title: DRA: DBC - scheduler behavior after binding failure
body:
## Summary

The `DRADeviceBindingConditions` feature requires that both `BindingConditions` and `BindingFailureConditions` are set as its specification. If the BindingFailureConditions are met, the scheduler will re-execute scheduling.

BindingFailureConditions are typically met when device preparation fails. Considering that such failures may be temporary, @dom4ha suggested allowing this feature to control scheduler's behavior so that, after re-scheduling, it can attempt to schedule the same device again.

In this issue, we will discuss the necessity of this enhancement and how it should be implemented.

Discussion link: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/5487#discussion_r2412008129

## Scenario

The following is the scenario assumed in this issue:

1. ResourceClaim is allocated to a device with BindingConditions.
2. An external controller detects this and performs device provisioning.
3. The provisioning fails for some reason and a BindingFailureConditions is marked on the ResourceClaim.
4. The scheduler initiates re-scheduling.

## **Proposed implementation ideas**

Introduce a well-known error status on binding failure and enable the scheduler to execute predefined actions based on that status. Specifically, implement the following statuses and behaviors in this statement.

- `retried` (on reschedule keep using the same device(s) if only they are still available as the failure could be transient),
- `reconsidered` (reassess all possible node options - the default behavior) or
- `avoided` (the same device can be still chosen but as the last option)

When `retried` is specified among the above, we could preserve the allocated resources for the next cycle but it's unclear how we'd grab the attached devices in the next cycle and needs further discussion.

## Necessity of This Enhancement

If a BindingFailure occurs and we want to reschedule on the same device, we need to preserve the allocation information for the next scheduling cycle; otherwise, we risk that the released resource will be taken by other pods, whether CPU, memory, or other required DRA resources.

@dom4ha  
I have summarized the points you suggested in the discussion link above. Please let me know if there is anything missing or that should be added. 

Also, I would like to discuss with other maintainers, including @pohly and @johnbelamaric, whether this enhancement is necessary or not.

title: Enhancement request: Allows paramsRef to check parameters on multiple namespace
body:
### What would you like to be added?

I would like to be able to pass on a `ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding.spec.paramRef` a matchNamespaces, and check for parameters on different namespaces.

Additionally with being able to matchNamespaces, I would like to be able to use resources on N namespaces as parameters. 

The parameters MUST be of the same type of the resource being validated (the same current behavior when matchSelector is passed today). I do not want to check different resource kinds



### Why is this needed?

As an example of a use case (please take this only as an example of usage!):
- I am an admin that allows users to create Ingress resources on any namespaces
- I want to be sure that once a user claims a hostname on an Ingress, another user on a different namespace will not be able to claim the same hostname

While I can make a controller or a webhook take care of it, it would be much more straightforward to use a VAP to limit this kind of situation.

I can achieve this today with a simple VAP/VAPB as
```
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
metadata:
  name: "demo-binding-test.example.com"
spec:
  policyName: "demo-policy.example.com"
  validationActions: [Deny]
  paramRef:
    selector: {}
    parameterNotFoundAction: Deny
  matchResources:
    namespaceSelector:
      matchLabels:
        env: test
---
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: "demo-policy.example.com"
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  paramKind:
    apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: Ingress
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:   ["networking.k8s.io"]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations:  ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
      resources:   ["ingresses"]
  variables:
  - name: objHostnames
    expression: "object.spec.rules.map(h, h.host)"
  - name: paramsHostnames
    expression: "params.spec.rules.map(h, h.host)"
  - name: hostnameExists
    expression: variables.objHostnames.all(item, item in variables.paramsHostnames)
  validations:
  - expression: "!variables.hostnameExists"
    message: "Hostname cannot be reused on a different object"
```

But this check happens only within the same namespace, while would be nice to be able to check also on different namespaces to avoid a hostname conflict (again, this is just a use case example).

I have created a PoC for the proposal at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/compare/master...rikatz:kubernetes:namespace-lister-on-policy

I understand that if this is accepted it will imply some KEP, feature gates, better testing, etc. Right now the idea is to make the proposal

Comments in the latter issue say that the issue has been fixed with the limit increased to 1024. If the above is true, then can the limitation be removed from the documentation?

Documentation needs update, no repro required.

body:
### What happened?

I'm interested in and testing the EnvFiles feature ([KEP-3721](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-node/3721-support-for-env-files/README.md)) and found that quote handling behavior is unclear and inconsistent with how ConfigMap handles quotes.

I may be misunderstanding something,
but I expected consistent quote handling behavior, similar to how ConfigMap works.

**Current behavior with EnvFiles:**

When using FileKeyRef with an env generated in initCoitainer:
```bash
SIMPLE=value
API_TOKEN='abc123'
DB_HOST="localhost"
JSON_DATA='{"key": "value"}'
```

The resulting environment variables include the quotes as literal characters:
```bash
SIMPLE=value                 # No quotes
API_TOKEN='abc123'           # Quotes preserved
DB_HOST="localhost"          # Quotes preserved  
JSON_DATA='{"key": "value"}' # Quotes preserved
```

**Comparison with ConfigMap:**

For reference, ConfigMap strips YAML quotes:
```yaml
data:
  API_TOKEN: "'abc123'"
  DB_HOST: "localhost"
  JSON_DATA: '{"key": "value"}'
  SIMPLE=value
```

Results in:
```bash
API_TOKEN='abc123'           # YAML outer quotes removed
DB_HOST=localhost            # YAML quotes removed
JSON_DATA={"key": "value"}   # YAML quotes removed
SIMPLE=value
```

**Documentation inconsistencies:**

1. KEP states: "[Values must be enclosed in single quotes (e.g., VAR='value').](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-node/3721-support-for-env-files/README.md#env-file)".
2. KEP also states: "[Any env file supported by k8s will yield the same environment variables as if it was interpreted by bash.](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-node/3721-support-for-env-files/README.md#env-file)"
3. [Official blog post](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2025/09/10/kubernetes-v1-34-env-files/#how-it-works) shows examples **without** quotes: `echo "CONFIG_VAR=HELLO" > /config/config.env`
4. Test cases only cover values `without` quotes

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected consistent quote handling behavior, similar to how ConfigMap works.
I want to know this difference is intentional or not.

ConfigMap strips quotes, but EnvFiles preserves them. For example:
```yaml
# ConfigMap
data:
  TOKEN: 'abc123'
# Result: TOKEN=abc123 (quotes removed)
```
```bash
# EnvFiles
TOKEN='abc123'
# Result: TOKEN='abc123' (quotes preserved)
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a test pod with EnvFiles:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: envfiles-test
spec:
  initContainers:
  - name: setup
    image: busybox
    command: 
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        cat > /data/config.env << 'EOF'
        API_TOKEN='abc123'
        DB_HOST="localhost"
        SIMPLE=value
        JSON='{"key": "value"}'
        EOF
    volumeMounts:
    - name: config
      mountPath: /data
  containers:
  - name: test
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
    env:
    - name: API_TOKEN
      valueFrom:
        fileKeyRef:
          path: config.env
          volumeName: config
          key: API_TOKEN
    - name: DB_HOST
      valueFrom:
        fileKeyRef:
          path: config.env
          volumeName: config
          key: DB_HOST
    - name: SIMPLE
      valueFrom:
        fileKeyRef:
          path: config.env
          volumeName: config
          key: SIMPLE
    - name: JSON
      valueFrom:
        fileKeyRef:
          path: config.env
          volumeName: config
          key: JSON
  volumes:
  - name: config
    emptyDir: {}
```

2. Check environment variables:
```bash
kubectl exec envfiles-test -- sh -c 'printf "API_TOKEN=[%s]\n" "$API_TOKEN"'
kubectl exec envfiles-test -- sh -c 'printf "DB_HOST=[%s]\n" "$DB_HOST"'
kubectl exec envfiles-test -- sh -c 'printf "SIMPLE=[%s]\n" "$SIMPLE"'
kubectl exec envfiles-test -- sh -c 'printf "JSON=[%s]\n" "$JSON"'
```

3. Observe that quotes are preserved in the values

### Why is this needed?

When it comes to gang scheduling, when Pod/Add event happens, it should also check unschedulable pods (because the newly added pod, along with unschedulable pods grouped together may complete the gang/workload).

title: kubelet TopologyManager Stalls on Large NUMA Systems (e.g. Nvidia GB200 Compute Tray with 34 NUMA nodes)
body:
### What happened?

When scheduling a pod (e.g. KubeVirt virt-launcher pod) that requests a PCI device on a very large NUMA system, kubelet’s TopologyManager never finishes computing topology hints and the pod is effectively stuck in admission:

- The pod is scheduled to the node.
- kubelet never reaches the device Allocate call for the requested resource.
- From a higher-level consumer (KubeVirt in our case), the virt-launcher pod stays in Pending and the VM remains in Starting with Ready = False.
- kubelet is responsive, but many goroutines are stuck in topology hint generation.

In our environment this manifests as:

- KubeVirt VM with a hostDevice (GPU, InfiniBand or NVMe) never transitions to Running, even though the node has the capacity and the device is free.
- Disabling TopologyManager or constraining the NUMA fan-out immediately lets the VM start

### What did you expect to happen?

kubelet should compute topology hints in bounded time, even on systems with many NUMA nodes (in a case GB200 with 34 NUMA nodes where only 2 NUMA nodes have CPUs, the rest are for HBM/NVLink), and call device-plugin Allocate so that pods/VMs using PCI host devices can start.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

## High-level repro:
1. Use a host with a large NUMA topology  
    Example: Nvidia GB200-class system with 34 NUMA nodes visible to the OS.
 
2. Run Kubernetes with kubelet configured roughly as follows:
```yaml
kubeReserved:
  cpu: "2"
  memory: 4Gi
  ephemeral-storage: 20Gi
systemReserved:
  cpu: "2"
  memory: 8Gi
  ephemeral-storage: 20Gi
topologyManagerPolicy: best-effort
topologyManagerScope: pod
topologyManagerPolicyOptions:
  prefer-closest-numa-nodes: "true"
  max-allowable-numa-nodes: "34"
cpuManagerPolicy: static
reservedSystemCPUs: "0-3,72-75"
cpuManagerPolicyOptions:
  distribute-cpus-across-numa: "false"
```
3. Deploy a device plugin that:
- Advertises a PCI resource (e.g. GPU, InfiniBand or NVMe) as a kubelet device resource.
- Exposes the device with topology information referencing many NUMA nodes (up to 34 in our case).

4. Create a Pod
Requests one unit of that device resource.
Uses Guaranteed QoS (requests == limits for CPU/memory) so that TopologyManager participates fully.
 
5. Observe
- The pod is scheduled to the node.
- kubelet never calls Allocate on the device plugin for that resource.
- The pod stays in Pending indefinitely.
- KubeVirt-specific repro (how we hit it)
- Instead of a raw pod, create a KubeVirt VirtualMachineInstance that uses hostDevices:
```yaml
devices:
   hostDevices:
    - deviceName: nvidia.com/GB100_HGX_GB200
      name: gpu1
```
The pod (if using KubeVirt, it is virt-launcher pod for a VM) is scheduled to the large NUMA node but stays Pending forever. The pod stuck at Pending, (if using KubeVirt, the VM status remains Starting) and never reaches Ready, despite sufficient resources.


### Anything else we need to know?

## Root cause analysis

- The kubelet TopologyManager asks each hint provider (CPU, memory, device) to compute topology hints over the set of NUMA nodes that the kubelet knows about.
- For the device plugin case, generateDeviceTopologyHints ends up calling bitmask.IterateBitMasks across a bitmask spanning all NUMA IDs known to the machine, not just those relevant to the requested device.
- With 34 NUMA nodes this becomes effectively an exponential search (O(2^n)) over the 34-bit mask.
- On a GB200 host with 34 NUMA nodes and a device plugin that advertises per-node topology across those nodes, generateDeviceTopologyHints spends unbounded time iterating combinations that are not actually schedulable for the requested device.
- While TopologyManager is doing this, kubelet never reaches the device Allocate call, so pods/VMs that need that device are permanently stuck in admission.

## Evidence observed

- Goroutine dumps from kubelet show many workers blocked under TopologyManager/device-manager paths, repeatedly calling IterateBitMasks on a large bitmask.
- No calls to Allocate are observed for the affected device resource while the system is in this hung state.
- If we disable TopologyManager, then virt-launcher pods immediately proceed and the KubeVirt VM starts successfully.

```console
$ kubectl version

Kustomize Version: v5.7.1

```

title: Kubelet fails to start on WSL2: "wrong number of fields" parsing /proc/mounts with Docker Desktop
body:
### What happened?

Kubelet fails to start on WSL2 when Docker Desktop is installed, with the error:

"Failed to start ContainerManager: system validation failed - wrong number of fields (expected at least 6, got 7)"

The root cause is in the parseProcMounts() function in staging/src/k8s.io/mount-utils/mount_linux.go. Docker Desktop on WSL2 creates mount entries with Windows paths containing unescaped spaces in the mount options field.

**Additional Info:**
The problematic mount entry from /proc/mounts:

C:\134Program\040Files\134Docker\134Docker\134resources /Docker/host 9p rw,noatime,aname=drvfs;path=C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\resources;symlinkroot=/mnt/,cache=5,access=client,msize=65536,trans=fd,rfd=3,wfd=3 0 0

The unescaped space in "path=C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\resources" causes strings.Fields() to split this into 7 fields instead of 6.

Verification:
$ cat /proc/mounts | awk '{print NF}' | sort -u
6
7

### What did you expect to happen?

Kubelet should start successfully on WSL2 with Docker Desktop installed. The /proc/mounts parser should handle mount entries where the options field contains unescaped spaces.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Install Windows with WSL2 and Docker Desktop for Windows with WSL2 backend enabled
2. Inside WSL2 Ubuntu, install Kubernetes components (kubeadm, kubelet, kubectl v1.34.2)
3. Join the WSL2 node to an existing Kubernetes cluster running on a separate Linux control-plane using kubeadm join
4. Observe kubelet fails to start with error: "Failed to start ContainerManager: system validation failed - wrong number of fields (expected 6, got 7)"

Root Cause:

Docker Desktop mounts Windows paths in WSL2's [mounts](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/mithu/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) with unescaped spaces in the options field

Example problematic entry:
C:\134Program\040Files\134Docker\134Docker\134resources /Docker/host 9p rw,noatime,aname=drvfs;path=C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\resources;symlinkroot=/mnt/,...


The options field contains path=C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\resources with unescaped spaces
When strings.Fields() parses this line, it splits on whitespace, creating 7-8 fields instead of the expected 6

To verify the problematic mount entry:
$ cat /proc/mounts | grep "Program Files"
 Check field count (should be 7-8 instead of 6)
$ cat /proc/mounts | grep "Program Files" | awk '{print NF}'

Key Point: This issue only occurs when WSL2 with Docker Desktop is used as a Kubernetes worker node joining a cluster. Running containers directly in WSL2 works fine - the issue is specific to kubelet's mounts parsing during node initialization.

### Anything else we need to know?

This affects WSL2 users who have Docker Desktop installed. The /proc/mounts format defines 6 fields (device, mountpoint, type, options, dump, pass), but the options field can contain unescaped spaces in 9p/drvfs filesystems used by WSL.

title: Make credential plugin policy/allowlist settable with `kubectl kuberc set`
body:
### What would you like to be added?

A new alpha command, `kubectl alpha kuberc set` has been added, which modifies the contents of the `kuberc` file. We should modify the interface to `kubectl alpha kuberc set` to make it possible to set the `credentialPluginPolicy` and `credentialPluginAllowlist` fields (added in 1.35 as an extension to KEP-3104) from the command line.

### Why is this needed?

This is needed in order to further reduce the friction for end-users in securing the `kubectl` client. `credentialPluginPolicy` and `credentialPluginAllowlist` are security knobs, and it would be great to have a simple cli one-liner to turn them on, rather than requiring the user to modify and/or create a new configuration file with which they may not be familiar.  In addition, the appropriate values may depend on provider configurations, but cloud providers can likewise provide CLI one-liners to allow their plugins but no others.

title: GKE Pod OOM Kills (Exit 137) - Next.js App Memory Leak Investigation
body:
### What happened?

Hello,

I'm troubleshooting recurring OOM kills (Exit Code 137) on GKE for a Next.js application. Looking for insights on memory management and debugging strategies.

**Environment:**
- Platform: GKE (Google Kubernetes Engine)
- Node Pool: Custom (node-pool=frontend)
- Container: Node.js 20.5.0 Alpine
- Image: Next.js 15.3.3 standalone build

**Pod Configuration:**

```yaml
Resources:
  Limits:
    cpu: 2800m
    memory: 3500Mi
  Requests:
    cpu: 2000m
    memory: 3000Mi

Environment:
  NODE_OPTIONS: --max-old-space-size=2048

Probes:
  Liveness: http-get :3000/api/health (delay=20s, period=10s)
  Readiness: http-get :3000/api/health (delay=20s, period=10s)
```

**Problem:**

Pods consistently OOM kill with Exit Code 137 after 5-11 hours of runtime. Pattern is accelerating (was 11h, now 5h).

**Timeline:**
```
Dec 3: 13:39 Start → 18:43 OOM (5h) → 05:49 OOM (11h)
Dec 4: 08:44 Start → 13:46 OOM (5h)
Restart Count: 8 (doubled in 24 hours)
```

**Observations:**

1. **Memory grows steadily:**
   - Starts: ~800MB
   - After 3h: ~2GB
   - After 5h: ~3.4GB → OOM

2. **Consistent pattern:**
   - Always Exit Code 137
   - No other errors in logs
   - Health checks pass until OOM

3. **High traffic:**
   - ~1,500-3,000 requests/hour
   - Mostly API calls to external service
   - Server-side rendering

**Logs Show:**

Frequent API calls to external service:

No errors, just normal operation until sudden OOM.

**Questions:**

1. **Is 3.5GB limit reasonable for Next.js SSR app?** Should I increase it or is this masking a leak?

2. **Heap limit vs Memory limit:** Currently heap=2GB, memory=3.5GB. Is this ratio correct?

3. **QoS Class is Burstable:** Should I make it Guaranteed by setting requests=limits?

4. **Node.js memory management:** Are there better NODE_OPTIONS for production?

5. **Monitoring:** What metrics should I track to catch this earlier?

**What I've Tried:**

- ✅ Increased memory from 3GB → 3.5GB (just delayed the problem)
- ✅ Added health endpoint with memory metrics
- ✅ Checked for memory leaks in application code
- ✅ Reviewed logs (no errors, just normal traffic)
- ❌ Cannot reproduce in local Docker (different traffic patterns)

**Questions for Community:**

1. Are there GKE-specific memory management settings I should check?
2. Should I enable memory profiling in production?
3. Are there better probe configurations for memory-intensive apps?
4. Should I implement pod disruption budgets?
5. Any recommended monitoring/alerting strategies?

**Current Mitigation:**

Considering:
- Increase memory to 5GB (temporary)
- Scale out to 6 replicas (distribute load)
- Implement pod auto-scaling based on memory

But want to fix root cause, not just mask it.

Any advice appreciated!


### What did you expect to happen?

The container pods should not get restarted once deployed.

NA

title: E2e test "should preempt lower priority pods using ReadWriteOncePod volumes" flakes
body:
### What happened?

We observed the e2e test `External Storage [Driver: disk.csi.azure.com] [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] read-write-once-pod [MinimumKubeletVersion:1.27] should preempt lower priority pods using ReadWriteOncePod volumes` causes flakes in other e2e tests in a downstream CI job with Azure Disk CSI driver.

[The test](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4e94e70dcad423e9f59f12ac5a048d2137d20e86/test/e2e/storage/testsuites/readwriteoncepod.go#L133) runs a default (low-prio) pod1 with a `ReadWriteOncePod` volume and then starts a high prio pod2 that tries to use the same volume. To run pod2, the scheduler has to evict pod1 to make the RWOP volume "free" for pod2. That works great, however, it may evict also pods of other e2e tests that run with the default priority.

What happened on a busy clusters, with all nodes at their attachment limit.

1. pod1 runs, pod2 is created.
2. The scheduler evicts pod1. That frees the RWOP volume and it also frees the last attachment slot on the node.
3. Some other e2e tests creates a Pod and scheduler puts it on the node, taking the last attachment slot.
4. The scheduler schedules pod2 agaian and it sees there is no node with a free attachment slot -> new round of eviction, now evicting a pod of unrelated e2e tests. The unrelated test will fail.  

We observed it with Azure, which can attach only 8 disks on the cheaper nodes, so it's more reproducible there.

### What did you expect to happen?

The preemption test should not affect other e2e tests

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

See above

title: SELinux warning controller reports conflicts for finished Pods
body:
### What happened?

The SELinux warning controller emits metrics + events when two pods that have different SELinux labels and share the same volume. This may not be supported when SELinuxMount feature gets GA. See the [KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-storage/1710-selinux-relabeling).

However, the controller reports these conflicting SELinux labels also for Pods in Failed or Succeeded phase. Kubelet is umounting volumes from these pods by default, so they cannot conflict with any other volume.

### What did you expect to happen?

The controller should ignore Succeeded and Failed pods.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run a pod that uses a PVC with SELinux label `s0:c0,c1` to completion (either Succeeded or Failed). Run a second pod that uses the same volume and has label `s0:c98,c99`. The controller now emits an event that these pods are conflicting. But the first one is finished and its volumes are unmounted, so they don't really conflict.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

title: [ac5c8895]
Block new `Disable*` feature gates
body:
Whilst working on issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/70585 and https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/53535 I formed a view that we should avoid having feature gates can have names that begin with "Disable".
We could add a CI/CD check that automatically points this out, because without automation it's just a guideline that people might now even have heard about.

That's my opinion, anyway. I hope this issue gets people agreeing with it.


Here's a sample of some Markdown that might help you see why the "Disable" prefix is harder to work with:


> When the feature gate `DisableCPUQuotaWithExclusiveCPUs` is enabled (the default), then Kubernetes
> does **not** enforce CPU quota for Pods that use the [Guaranteed](https://k8s.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-qos/#guaranteed) QoS class.
> 
> You can disable the `DisableCPUQuotaWithExclusiveCPUs` feature gate to restore the legacy behavior.

Basically, the double negatives are uncomfortable to explain, tricky to learn, and they are not fun to localize either (in some languages, a double negative is still a negative; in others, it's like code and it's a positive).

The obvious fix is to rename the feature gate and invert the sense, eg to have a feature gate that is named `LegacyCPUQuotaEnforcementWithExclusiveCPUs`, and that is **off** by default. But we could really use some automation to point this out to people, rather than relying on (eg) SIG Architecture to point it out, or SIG Docs when people try to document it.

---

Before we make an automation change, let's update [`contributors/devel/sig-architecture/feature-gates.md`](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/82b8a1affb3376d0fa1e8f381d4847680bbbba41/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/feature-gates.md) in [k/community](https://github.com/kubernetes/community) to recommend that people don't start the names of gates with "Disable".

(and before _that_, we should wait for this issue to be triaged as accepted)


/sig architecture
/kind feature

title: kubelet_http_requests_duration_seconds metric records incorrect (near-zero) latency values
body: ### What happened? The `kubelet_http_requests_duration_seconds` histogram metric always records near-zero values (~2 microseconds) regardless of actual request processing time. Below is a screenshot from a downstream CI run showing the average latency of kubetet's /metrics/cadvisor endpoint: ### What did you expect to happen? The metric should record the actual time taken to handle each HTTP request, from when it's received until the response is sent. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? 1. Make an HTTP request to the kubelet that takes a measurable amount of time (e.g., `/pods/` endpoint) 2. Query the `kubelet_http_requests_duration_seconds` metric 3. Observe that the recorded duration is always ~2 microseconds instead of the actual processing time ### Anything else we need to know? **Root cause:** In `pkg/kubelet/server/server.go`, the defer statement evaluates `SinceInSeconds(startTime)` immediately when the defer is declared, not when it executes: ```go defer servermetrics.HTTPRequestsDuration.WithLabelValues(...).Observe(servermetrics.SinceInSeconds(startTime)) ``` In Go, arguments to deferred function calls are evaluated immediately at the defer statement. This means `SinceInSeconds(startTime)` computes the duration at the start of the request (~5µs after `startTime` was set), rather than at the end when the defer actually runs. This affects observability and SLO tracking for kubelet HTTP endpoints since duration data is meaningless. ### Kubernetes version 1.33

title: Missing request total apiserver latency and components break down in the audit log annotation
body:
### What happened?

Missing request total apiserver latency and components break down in the audit log annotation causes trouble when we want to narrow down which component took longer for a specific slow request. 

In the audit http filter, `writeLatencyToAnnotation` will track latency in annotation only when the total latency of the given request exceeds 500ms. The total latency is calculated by subtracting request start time `ac.GetEventRequestReceivedTimestamp().Time` from end time `ac.GetEventStageTimestamp()`. 

However, the end time is not assigned until the audit log event is persisted to the audit backend [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/612122f1d79eb148b06bb63fbf392c03f9b73d60/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/filters/audit.go#L107)

The issue was probably introduced in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129472

audit log with latency annotation when the request latency exceeds 500ms

title: Kubelet fails to clean up subPath volumes for pods force-deleted while kubelet was stopped
body:
### What happened?

When the kubelet on a node is stopped and a pod using a `hostPath` volume mounted via `subPath` is force-deleted (e.g., with `kubectl delete --force`), the kubelet fails to clean up the corresponding subpath directory at `/var/lib/kubelet/pods/<pod-uid>/volume-subpaths/` upon restart.

After restart, kubelet detects the orphaned pod and repeatedly logs messages like:
```
orphaned pod \"xxxx\" found, but failed to rmdir() subpath at path /var/lib/kubelet/pods/xxxx/volume-subpaths/xxxx: remove /var/lib/kubelet/pods/xxxx/volume-subpaths/xxxx: device or resource busy
```

### What did you expect to happen?

After kubelet restarts, the directories associated with the force-deleted pod—including its subPath volume mounts under `/var/lib/kubelet/pods/<pod-uid>/`—should be properly cleaned up, and no recurring error logs about orphaned subpaths should appear.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a pod that uses a hostPath volume mounted via subPath.
2. Stop the kubelet on the node where the pod is running.
3. Force-delete the pod using kubectl delete --force.
4. Restart the kubelet.

title: Implement Quota Scope for Label Resource Exclusion
body:
#### What would you like to be added

Extend the ResourceQuota quota scopes mechanism to support excluding Pods and PVCs from quota accounting based on specific labels.
This would enable workloads to mark resources that should not consume quota (e.g., temporary resources during migration or import operations).

Implement [new Quota Scope](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/apis/core/types.go#L6447): `ObjectLabel` managed by resources.k8s.io/ignore annotation on pod/pvc
#### Why is this needed:

Current ResourceQuota scopes [provide](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/resource-quotas/#quota-scopes) limited filtering capabilities. Many use cases require the ability to temporarily exclude resources from quota without modifying application code or resource definitions:
1. **VM/Pod Migration Workflows**: When migrating VMs(pods as virtual machines), a second Pod is created during the migration process. This temporary Pod should not be counted toward the namespace quota until the migration is complete.
2. **Storage Import Operations**: Temporary PVCs created during disk import should not count against storage quotas.
3. **Ephemeral Resources**: Controllers managing temporary resources need a way to mark them as exempt from quota accounting dynamically, even after the resource is created.

It's also worth mentioning #77508 and #110065 with a similar request, here we complement the user case and are ready to help with its implementation.

We can offer several options for implementation for scope usage:

Filter directly by labels:
```yaml
scopeSelector: 
  matchExpressions: 
  - operator: NotIn 
     scopeName: ObjectLabel 
     values: ["workload-type=migration"]
```
We are open to discussion

title: "Netpol" e2e tests are still too resource-intensive
body:
The "Netpol" tests in `test/e2e/network/netpol` are extremely resource intensive. (They used to be even worse, but they were improved at some point.) In particular, there are 48 tests that each launch 9 pods (sometimes with multiple containers per pod). With heavy ginkgo parallelism, this can result in a ton of I/O.

Some improvements that could be made:

- [x] Limit the Netpol tests to a single container per pod.
  - `agnhost serve-hostname` (which is currently used for TCP and UDP serving) can only serve a single port/protocol, but `agnhost porter` (which is currently used for SCTP serving) can serve many ports from a single process. #135706 was an attempt to rewrite it to always use `agnhost port`, but it doesn't work because it turns out `agnhost porter` doesn't currently support UDP. So, (1) add UDP serving support to agnhost, (2) probably also make it so you can say `SERVE_TCP_PORT_X` in addition to `SERVE_PORT_X`, just for consistency, (3) get new agnhost images built, update the e2e agnhost dependency, (4) revive #135706 (and make sure it works; it's still untested).
  - Fixed by @ShaanveerS: #135911, #136474
- [x] Reduce the number of pods per test in Netpol.
  - Right now it creates 3 namespaces with 3 pods in each namespace, but literally none of the tests actually need all 9 pods. For example:
    - `"should support a 'default-deny-ingress' policy"` needs to test that (1) 2 pods in namespace X can't connect to each other, (2) a pod in namespace Y can't connect to a pod in namespace X, (3) a pod in namespace X or Y _can_ connect to a pod in namespace Y. So that requires 4 pods, 2 in namespace X, and 2 in namespace Y.
    - `"should enforce policy to allow ingress traffic for a target"` tests a deny-all policy plus an "allow from any to A" policy in namespace X. So it would also need 4 pods to be exhaustive (everything can connect to x/a, nothing can connect to x/b, everything can connect to y/a and y/b). However, if we assume that the first test case proves that a policy in namespace X doesn't affect Y-to-Y traffic, then we could get away with only 3 pods here (dropping y/b).
    - `"should enforce policy to allow traffic only from a different namespace, based on NamespaceSelector"` needs all 3 namespaces (to include "the namespace that is the target of the policy", "the namespace that is the peer of the policy", and "another namespace not referred to by the policy", but it can get by with 4 pods total (x/a, x/b, y/a, z/a).
  - A simple fix would be to shrink it down to "3 pods in X, 2 in Y, 1 in Z" (after confirming that that does provide enough coverage to ensure the right behavior in each test).
  - A larger fix would be changing `NewModel` etc to allow specify exactly which pods you need (e.g., `[]string{"x/a", "x/b", "y/a", "z/a"}`; I think changing `Model` to work with the namespace name suffixes (x, y, z) rather than the full namespace names would simplify a bunch of things.)
    - Implemented by @ShaanveerS in #137110
- [ ] Remove redundant / non-useful Netpol tests
- [ ] Maybe others?

If someone wants to work on any of these, I can give more guidance.

/sig network
/priority important-longterm
/area testing
/help

title: Kubelet retries NodeStageVolume indefinitely on NOT_FOUND
body:
### What happened?

When a CSI driver's `NodeStageVolume` returns `NOT_FOUND` (gRPC code 5), the kubelet continuously retries the operation with exponential backoff. However, the kubelet does not perform the recovery behavior specified in the CSI spec for this error code.

This results in pods being stuck in `ContainerCreating` state indefinitely, requiring manual intervention.

### What did you expect to happen?

According to the [CSI spec for NodeStageVolume errors](https://github.com/container-storage-interface/spec/blob/master/spec.md#nodestagevolume-errors), when `NOT_FOUND` is returned:

> **Condition:** Volume does not exist.
>
> **gRPC Code:** `5 NOT_FOUND`
>
> **Recovery Behavior:** "Caller MUST verify that the `volume_id` is correct and that the volume is accessible and has not been deleted before retrying with exponential back off."

The kubelet should follow this recovery behavior: **verify that the volume is accessible** before retrying.

Currently, the kubelet only retries `NodeStageVolume` without any verification step, which does not comply with the CSI spec.



### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Deploy a CSI driver that returns `NOT_FOUND` from `NodeStageVolume` when the volume device is not present on the node
2. Create a PVC and a Pod that mounts it
3. Cause the volume to become inaccessible (e.g., detach via cloud API, node reboot, storage issue)
4. Observe:
   - Pod stuck in `ContainerCreating`
   - Kubelet retries `NodeStageVolume` indefinitely
   - No verification of volume accessibility as specified by CSI spec

title: `kubectl describe service` does not display `appProtocol` field
body:
## Problem

The `appProtocol` field (GA since v1.20) is not displayed in `kubectl describe service` output, even when set. Users must use `kubectl get svc -o yaml` to verify this field.

This can be problematic when debugging Service Mesh or Gateway API configurations where `appProtocol` affects traffic routing. Given that `appProtocol` has been GA for several years and is actively used in Service Mesh environments, displaying it in `kubectl describe` output would be beneficial for users.

## Proposed Solution

Display `appProtocol` in the port section of `kubectl describe service` output:
```
Port:              http  80/TCP
TargetPort:        8080/TCP
AppProtocol:       http          # <-- Add this
NodePort:          http  30080/TCP
```

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go#L3015

## Benefits

- Consistency with other port fields (`name`, `protocol`, `port`, `targetPort`, `nodePort`)
- Easier debugging for Service Mesh and Gateway API users

title: Update vendored hnslib to v0.1.2 in Kubernetes
body:
**Description**

Kubernetes currently vendors an older version of hnslib for Windows networking / kube-proxy functionality. We would like to update the vendored version to hnslib v0.1.2.

This update brings important improvements for Windows kube-proxy and HNS interactions and aligns Kubernetes with the latest upstream hnslib.

**Motivation / Problem Statement**

Windows kube-proxy relies on hnslib (via hcsshim) for programming HNS networks, load balancers, and policies.

The currently vendored version is missing several fixes and enhancements that are available in hnslib v0.1.2, resulting in limited functionality and additional maintenance burden in Kubernetes.

**Major Updates in hnslib v0.1.2**

The following are the key changes introduced in hnslib v0.1.2 that motivate this update:

- **Dropped archived dependency**: Removed the deprecated and archived dependency: `github.com/pkg/errors` in favor of standard Go error handling.
- **Updated to latest HNS version:** hnslib is updated to work with the latest HNS APIs, including support for ModifyLoadBalancerPolicy, which allows updating existing load balancer policies instead of delete-and-recreate flows.
- **Added flags field to Network Subnets**: Introduced a flags field for network subnets, enabling additional configurability and better parity with evolving HNS capabilities.

These updates improve stability, correctness, and extensibility of Windows networking in Kubernetes.

**Proposal**

- Update the vendored hnslib dependency in Kubernetes to v0.1.2
- Ensure all Windows kube-proxy and networking components compile and function correctly
- Validate changes through existing Windows CI and targeted testing

**Scope**

- Component: `Windows kube-proxy / Windows networking`
- SIGs involved:
```
sig/windows

sig/network
```

**Expected Impact**

- No behavior change for Linux nodes
- Improved stability and functionality for Windows kube-proxy
- Enables future improvements that depend on HNS ModifyLoadBalancerPolicy support
- Reduced technical debt by removing archived dependencies

**Risks and Mitigations**

Risk: API or behavior changes in hnslib v0.1.2
Mitigation: Validate via Windows CI and manual testing on supported Windows Server versions.

**Kubernetes Version**

Affects: main branch

Backporting can be evaluated for supported release branches if appropriate

title: Analysis of Kubelet Init Container Restart Count Issue
body:
### What happened?

The user created a pod with an init container. After the init container was created but before it started, the system rebooted.

After the system rebooted, clock synchronization was performed, causing the time to jump forward by several tens of seconds. At this point, the kubelet recreated the sandbox and init container and started it. The start time of the newly launched init container was earlier than that of the init container in the "created" state that existed before the reboot.

During subsequent operations, the status of the init container was retrieved, but it corresponded to the container created before the reboot. When attempting to create a new one, the restart count of the container was actually undercounted by 1. This caused the newly created container to have the same sequence number as the one after the reboot, preventing it from starting at all.

I am not sure whether this qualifies as an issue.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/container/runtime.go#L424-L433
```golang
// FindContainerStatusByName returns container status in the pod status with the given name.
// When there are multiple containers' statuses with the same name, the first match will be returned.

	for _, containerStatus := range podStatus.ContainerStatuses {
		if containerStatus.Name == containerName {
			return containerStatus

	return nil
}
```

pod can be run normal

title: Workload API gaps for disaggregated/multi-component inference workloads
body:
### Overview
The current Workload API in KEP-4671 supports intra-PodGroup gang scheduling effectively - all pods within a PodGroup (or PodGroup replica) can be required to schedule together. However, the design treats each `PodGroup` or `PodGroup` replica as fully independent scheduling units, which creates several gaps for workloads that require coordination across groups or replicas.

From the KEP:
> The individual PodGroups and PodGroup replicas are treated as independent gangs.
> As an example, if one of the groups can be scheduled and the other can't be - this is exactly what will happen.

The intent of this issue is to highlight these gaps and start a discussion, not to propose specific API changes or fixes. Additionally the gaps are explained in the context of disaggregated inference to ground them but are general gaps that would come up in a variety of AI workloads.

### Motivating Use Case: Disaggregated LLM Inference
In disaggregated inference architectures (prefill-decode separation), a functional serving instance requires both:
* **Prefill workers:** Handle prompt processing
* **Decode workers:** Handle token generation

A deployment is only functional if it has at least one of **each** worker type. These worker types may be single-node (representable by a Deployment or StatefulSet) or multi-node (representable by LWS or Grove PodCliqueScalingGroup). The gaps described below prevent expressing the scheduling requirements for these deployments.

### Gap 1: Inconsistent Semantics for `minCount` Across Single-Node vs Multi-Node Workers
The current API has inconsistent semantics for `minCount` depending on whether workers are single-node or multi-node.

* **Single-node case (e.g., Deployment or StatefulSet):** If I have a Deployment as a PodGroup where each replica is a single pod, I can assign all pods to the same PodGroup with the same (or no) `podGroupReplicaKey`. In this case, `minCount` effectively represents the minimum number of **replicas** I need scheduled.
* **Multi-node case (e.g., LeaderWorkerSet or Grove PodCliqueScalingGroup):** If I have an LWS as a PodGroup where each replica consists of multiple pods, the controller is expected to assign each pod a `podGroupReplicaKey` to distinguish replicas. In this case, `minCount` represents how many pods within a single LWS replica need to be scheduled - **not** how many LWS replicas need to be scheduled.

**Impact:** The semantics of `minCount` differ based on whether the PodGroup is representing a single-node or multi-node component, and there is no way to express "I need at least N complete multi-node replicas" for the LWS case. To me, this inconsistency is something that is important to address immediately as opposed to the fix being purely additive.

### Gap 2: No Inter-PodGroup Gang Constraints
Even if Gap 1 is addressed, there is no way to tie together minimum requirements across PodGroups into an all-or-nothing scheduling unit.

#### Single-node example
Even when replicas of prefill and decode workers are single pods, I cannot express "schedule at least 1 prefill pod AND at least 1 decode pod, or none at all." The current API allows me to guarantee that I get a given number of prefill pods or none, and a given number of decode pods or none, but these are independent guarantees. There is no way to express that I need at least 1 of each or none at all.

* *Risk:* The scheduler might schedule 10 prefill pods and 0 decode pods, resulting in a non-functional deployment.

#### Multi-node example
When workers themselves require multiple pods (e.g., a prefill worker spans 4 nodes for tensor parallelism), two levels of gang scheduling are needed:
1.  **Intra-group:** All pods within a single worker replica must schedule together
2.  **Inter-group:** At least 1 complete prefill replica AND at least 1 complete decode replica must schedule together, or none at all

The current API allows me to express intra-group constraints, but not the inter-group constraint that ties them together. Hierarchical gang scheduling is not supported, though adding support likely could be done in a purely additive way unlike gap 1.

> **Implied Requirement:** Scheduler should work to satisfy minimum requirements for all PodGroups before allocating resources beyond them.
> For instance if my application needs at least 1 prefill + 1 decode to function, but ideally wants 4 prefill + 2 decode, a situation should not occur where I schedule 2 prefills before I schedule 1 decode and then falsely end up failing scheduling for the entire workload when 1 prefill + 1 decode would’ve succeeded.

### Future Consideration: Hierarchical Topology Scheduling
This is less of a gap and more of a forward-looking consideration. The KEP mentions synergy between gang scheduling and topology-aware scheduling. As these features evolve, we should keep in mind that hierarchical topology requirements will emerge:

* **Topology requirements at the functional unit level:** The entire deployment (prefill + decode together) may have topology constraints - for instance the whole deployment being within a block.
* **Topology requirements at the PodGroup level:** Individual PodGroups like prefill or decode may have their own topology constraints - for instance each prefill worker being on the same nvl72 rack.
* **Cross-group affinity:** There may be preferences for scheduling prefill workers topologically closer to decode workers rather than to other prefill workers.

These requirements mirror the hierarchical nature of gang scheduling and should be considered as the API evolves.

title: Go 1.24.11 and 1.25.5 Cannot Build Projects Using Kubernetes Due to gogo/protobuf
body:
### What happened?

Projects using Kubernetes client libraries cannot upgrade to Go 1.24.11 or 1.25.5, which include fixes for **CVE-2025-61729** (crypto/x509), because these versions fail during `go mod tidy`/`go mod vendor` with gogo/protobuf errors.


## Affected Versions

**Go versions with CVE-2025-61729 fix (FAIL with Kubernetes):**
- Go 1.24.11
- Go 1.25.5

**Last working Go versions (VULNERABLE to CVE-2025-61729):**
- Go 1.24.10
- Go 1.25.4

**Kubernetes versions tested:**
- k8s.io/client-go v0.33.1
- k8s.io/client-go v0.34.1

Both Kubernetes versions fail with Go 1.24.11 and Go 1.25.5 due to stricter module validation that correctly identifies gogo/protobuf's broken module structure.

## Root Cause

- `gogo/protobuf` has broken module structure
- Go 1.24.11 and 1.25.5 include stricter module validation (correct behavior)
- Kubernetes still depends on `gogo/protobuf` (via `openshift/api` and others)

## Questions

1. **When will Kubernetes complete the gogo/protobuf removal?**
2. **Which Kubernetes version will be compatible with Go 1.24.11 and 1.25.5?**
3. **What should projects do about CVE-2025-61729 in the meantime?**

## Impact

- **CVE-2025-61729:** crypto/x509 vulnerability (Certificate.Verify and Certificate.VerifyHostname)
- **Fixed in:** Go 1.24.11 and Go 1.25.5 (December 2, 2025)
- **Problem:** Cannot apply these fixes while using Kubernetes v0.33.x or v0.34.x
- **Compliance:** Security scanners flag CVE-2025-61729, blocking compliance audits
- **Scope:** Affects all projects using k8s.io/client-go, k8s.io/api, k8s.io/apimachinery

## Request

This is a critical security blocker. Please provide:
1. Timeline for gogo/protobuf removal
2. Compatible Kubernetes version
3. Guidance for projects that need both current K8s and CVE fixes

## Related

- CVE-2025-61729 - https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2025-3468

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected `go mod tidy` and `go mod vendor` to succeed when using Go 1.24.11 
or Go 1.25.5 with Kubernetes v0.33.1 and v0.34.1, just as they work with 
earlier Go versions (1.24.10 and 1.25.4).

Projects should be able to upgrade to the latest Go patch releases to receive 
critical security fixes (like CVE-2025-61729) without breaking their Kubernetes 
dependencies.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

## Reproduction

```bash
mkdir /tmp/k8s-go-test && cd /tmp/k8s-go-test

cat > go.mod << 'EOF'
module example.com/k8s-test
go 1.24.11
require (
    k8s.io/api v0.33.1
    k8s.io/apimachinery v0.33.1
    k8s.io/client-go v0.33.1
)
EOF

cat > main.go << 'EOF'
package main
import (
    corev1 "k8s.io/api/core/v1"
    "fmt"
)
func main() {
    fmt.Println(&corev1.Pod{})
}
EOF

go mod tidy  # Fails with Go 1.24.11 or 1.25.5
```

```
go: module github.com/gogo/protobuf@latest found (v1.3.2),
```

title: Kubelet restart causes NotReady pod to be briefly marked Ready before probe workers exist
body:
### What happened?

When kubelet restarts, there is a race condition in `prober_manager.go` that causes pods that were NOT Ready before the restart to be briefly marked as Ready. This happens because:

1. During `SyncPod`, `UpdatePodStatus` is called before prober workers are created
2. The code assumes "no worker exists = no readiness probe configured" and marks the container Ready
3. The pod is updated to Ready in the API server
4. Prober workers are then created and the first probe runs
5. The probe fails and the pod is marked NotReady again

This brief Ready window (we observed ~4 seconds) is enough for PodDisruptionBudget checks to succeed, allowing evictions that should have been blocked.

### Code Location

In `pkg/kubelet/prober/prober_manager.go`, the `UpdatePodStatus` function (around line 350):

```go
} else {
    // The check whether there is a probe which hasn't run yet.
    w, exists := m.getWorker(pod.UID, c.Name, readiness)
    ready = !exists // no readinessProbe -> always ready
```

The comment says "no readinessProbe -> always ready" but `exists` is false in TWO cases:
1. No readiness probe configured (intended)
2. Prober worker hasn't been created yet after kubelet restart (potential bug)

### Timeline from Production Incident

| Time (UTC) | Event | Source |
|------------|-------|--------|
| 05:13:53 | Pod marked NOT Ready | Kubelet logs |
| 05:14:25 | Kubelet stops and restarts | systemd logs |
| 05:14:26 | Pod marked **Ready** | API server audit logs |
| 05:14:29 | Another pod eviction **succeeds** | API server audit logs |
| 05:14:30 | Pod marked NOT Ready | API server audit logs |

The pod was Ready for only 4 seconds, but this was enough for Karpenter (retrying evictions) to successfully evict another pod, causing two pods to be down simultaneously despite PDB `maxUnavailable: 1`.

### Why KEP-4781 Doesn't Fix This

[KEP-4781](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/4781-kublet-restart-pod-status) addresses the opposite problem (Ready→NotReady after restart). 

Looking at [scenario-1.png](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/raw/master/keps/sig-node/4781-kublet-restart-pod-status/scenario-1.png) from the KEP:

1. During "First SyncPod Execution", the pod is marked Ready=true and API server is updated
2. The fix's precondition for "First Probe Execution" is "container Ready status is true"
3. But for pods that were NOT Ready before restart, the damage is already done - the API server was updated with Ready=true during SyncPod

The KEP fix preserves Ready status for pods that WERE Ready. It doesn't prevent the incorrect Ready=true update during SyncPod for pods that were NOT Ready.

### What did you expect to happen?

Pods that were NOT Ready before kubelet restart should remain NOT Ready until probes pass. The kubelet should not assume "no worker = no probe configured" immediately after restart.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. Create a pod with a readiness probe that initially fails (e.g., checks for a file that doesn't exist)
2. Wait for pod to be marked NotReady
3. Restart kubelet on that node
4. Observe the pod briefly becoming Ready before the first probe runs and fails

### Anything else we need to know?

**Suggested Fix:**
During `UpdatePodStatus` after kubelet restart, if:
- No probe result exists in readinessManager
- No probe worker exists yet
- But the pod spec HAS a readiness probe configured

Then the container should be marked NOT Ready (or preserve the previous Ready state from API server) rather than assuming Ready.

### Kubernetes version

Observed in production on EKS 1.33. Code analysis shows the issue exists in current master.

### Cloud provider

AWS (EKS)

### OS version

Amazon Linux 2023

### Related Issues

- #100277 - Pod temporarily reports containerNotReady after restart (opposite direction)
- #78733 - Pod with readinessProbe becomes not ready on restart (opposite direction)
- KEP-4781 - Kubelet Restart Pod Status (addresses opposite problem)

title: TopologySpreadConstraint should fail if labelSelector not provided
body:
So I've just recently realized, and folks can confirm - that if you create a TopologySpreadConstraint but do not list a `labelSelector`, it will be accepted - but will effectively do nothing since it matches nothing.

At least my observation was it was not respected until I added the `labelSelector`.

e.g. something like:
```
topologySpreadConstraints:
  - maxSkew: 1
    topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/hostname
    whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
```

actually needs to be:
```
topologySpreadConstraints:
  - maxSkew: 1
    topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/hostname
    whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
    labelSelector:
      matchLabels:
        app: my-app
```

Unless I'm missing something, it seems clear to me that no one would want to specify a constraint without also having a `labelSelector` - and seems easy to miss.

I already missed it for my own application, and another application I use (cockroachDB), [also seems to have missed it](https://github.com/cockroachdb/helm-charts/blob/65fa4c6822b18d3cd8922cca60393199b7d95edb/cockroachdb-parent/charts/cockroachdb/values.yaml#L439) ([fix](https://github.com/cockroachdb/helm-charts/pull/584)).

While we are here - a related matter I find interesting, is that you can not specify `matchLabelKeys` without `labelSelector` (as per the [docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.34/#topologyspreadconstraint-v1-core)). Assuming I understand how it works, it seems like a pretty standard default to just want to match against key "app", whatever it is for my pod - and that's it.

Perhaps more generally, errors could be reported if labelSelector / matchLabelKeys ends up finding nothing (including itself!).

title: HNS loadbalancers for services are not recreated
body:
### What happened?

HNS loadbalancers appear to persist in cache, if removed these are never created throughout the lifecycle of kube-proxy. This out-of-band cleanup of loadbalancers could occur during service restarts of kubelet a CNI or race condition with another service.

Similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133928 however this issue applies to all service types. Reproduction has occurred using the default `internalTrafficPolicy: Cluster`



### What did you expect to happen?

kube-proxy invalidates cache and recreates missing HNS loadbalancers to avoid service disruption

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This has been known to occur during rke2 service restarts, the simplest reproduction is a manual removal of a loadbalancer:

On a Windows worker node:
- List the load balancers: `hnsdiag list loadbalancers`
  - Example:
  ```
  Load Balancer    : 3599612c-54b4-4b9d-9258-4fc5e2100549
    Virtual IPs      : 172.30.0.1
    Direct IP IDs    : 78c19c4d-7edf-43bd-ab2a-5ccf97f214fe
  ```

- Select an LB to remove: `hnsdiag delete loadbalancers <ID>`
  - Example:
  ```
  > hnsdiag delete loadbalancers 3599612c-54b4-4b9d-9258-4fc5e2100549
  ```
- Monitor the LB list, and kube-proxy logs:
  - `hnsdiag list loadbalancers`
  - In kube-proxy logs the LB is persisted in a cache:
  ```
  I1217 23:36:36.438104    7712 proxier.go:1225] "Policy already applied" serviceInfo="172.30.0.1:443/TCP"
  ```

The kube-proxy sync interval continues to log that the policy is applied, yet the loadbalancers list has no matching LB. Restarting kube-proxy will rebuild the loadbalancers.

title: Kubelet SyncTerminatedPod times out after 30s due to race with cleanupOrphanedPodCgroups
body:
### What happened?

In this [OpenShift CI run](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results/logs/periodic-ci-openshift-multiarch-master-nightly-4.21-ocp-e2e-ovn-remote-s2s-libvirt-ppc64le/1999572809340162048), the upstream `[sig-node] Lifecycle sleep action zero value when create a pod with lifecycle hook using sleep action with a duration of zero seconds prestop hook using sleep action with zero duration` test failed because SyncTerminatedPod timed out. The kubelet logs shows:

```
Dec 12 21:19:08.719197 compute-1 kubenswrapper[7200]: E1212 21:19:08.719175    7200 pod_workers.go:1324] "Error syncing pod, skipping" err="failed to delete cgroup paths for [kubepods besteffort poda4418b44-5c5a-4bd5-b7b3-42860ff00483] : unable to destroy cgroup paths for cgroup [kubepods besteffort poda4418b44-5c5a-4bd5-b7b3-42860ff00483] : Timed out while waiting for systemd to remove kubepods-besteffort-poda4418b44_5c5a_4bd5_b7b3_42860ff00483.slice" pod="e2e-pod-lifecycle-sleep-action-allow-zero-761/pod-with-prestop-sleep-hook-zero-duration" podUID="a4418b44-5c5a-4bd5-b7b3-42860ff00483"
```

The systemd journal reveals that the slice was actually removed successfully ~30 seconds before the kubelet timeout:

```
Dec 12 21:18:39.127974 compute-1 systemd[1]: Removed slice libcontainer container kubepods-besteffort-poda4418b44_5c5a_4bd5_b7b3_42860ff00483.slice.
```

This shows that systemd completed the slice removal at 21:18:39, but kubelet still timed out at 21:19:08 (exactly ~30 seconds later). The timeout occurred because the kubelet goroutine that initiated the removal never received the D-Bus completion signal.

### What did you expect to happen?

Pod deletion should complete promptly after containers terminate, without a 30-second timeout.

### How can we reproduce it? (as minimally and precisely as possible)

1. Create a cluster with cgroupsPerQOS enabled (default)
2. Run a workload that creates and deletes many pods rapidly
3. Observe that some pods take 30+ seconds to fully terminate

The race is more likely to occur when:
- Multiple pods are being terminated simultaneously
- The orphaned pod cgroup cleanup housekeeping runs during pod termination

### Anything else we need to know?

#### Root Cause

There is a race condition between two code paths that call `pcm.Destroy()` on the same pod cgroup:

1. **`SyncTerminatedPod`** - [pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c34c5a5426aeb48c55c40af5c4b016a71c24d2d1/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2398-L2402):
```go
pcm := kl.containerManager.NewPodContainerManager()
if err := pcm.Destroy(name); err != nil {
    return err
}
```

2. **`cleanupOrphanedPodCgroups`** - [pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c34c5a5426aeb48c55c40af5c4b016a71c24d2d1/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L2835-L2836):
```go
go pcm.Destroy(val)
```

Both paths can run concurrently for the same pod cgroup. The `Destroy()` method calls systemd's `StopUnit` via D-Bus using `go-systemd`.

#### Why the 30-second timeout occurs

When `StopUnitContext` is called, the `go-systemd` library:

1. Sends a D-Bus method call to systemd's `StopUnit`
2. Systemd returns a **job path** (e.g., `/org/freedesktop/systemd1/job/12345`)
3. The library registers the caller's `statusChan` in an internal map keyed by that job path
4. When systemd emits a `JobRemoved` D-Bus signal with that job path, the library sends the result to the registered channel

**The problem:** When two goroutines call `StopUnit` on the same unit concurrently, systemd may return the **same job path** for both requests (since it's already processing a stop for that unit). The `go-systemd` library overwrites the first channel registration:

[go-systemd/dbus/methods.go](https://github.com/coreos/go-systemd/blob/f3c9410fa503128ff5a025265768843eb09815ca/dbus/methods.go#L55-L75
)
```go
// In go-systemd's dbus/methods.go (simplified)
func (c *Conn) startJob(ch chan<- string, job dbus.ObjectPath) {
    c.jobListener.Lock()
    c.jobListener.jobs[job] = ch  // OVERWRITES any existing channel for this job path!
    c.jobListener.Unlock()
}
```

**Timeline of the race:**

1. **T=0ms:** Goroutine A calls `StopUnit`, gets job `/job/100`, registers `chanA`
2. **T=1ms:** Goroutine B calls `StopUnit`, gets job `/job/100`, registers `chanB` (overwrites `chanA`!)
3. **T=50ms:** Systemd finishes, emits `JobRemoved` for `/job/100`
4. **T=50ms:** go-systemd sends result to `chanB` (the only one in the map now)
5. **T=50ms:** Goroutine B completes successfully
6. **T=30s:** Goroutine A times out (`chanA` was orphaned, never receives signal)

#### Relevant code

The 30-second timeout is in [opencontainers/cgroups/systemd/common.go](https://github.com/opencontainers/cgroups/blob/main/systemd/common.go#L184-L210):

```go
func stopUnit(cm *dbusConnManager, unitName string) error {
    statusChan := make(chan string, 1)
    err := cm.retryOnDisconnect(func(c *systemdDbus.Conn) error {
        _, err := c.StopUnitContext(context.TODO(), unitName, "replace", statusChan)
        return err
    })
    if err == nil {
        timeout := time.NewTimer(30 * time.Second)
        defer timeout.Stop()

        select {
        case s := <-statusChan:
            // ...
        case <-timeout.C:
            return errors.New("Timed out while waiting for systemd to remove " + unitName)
        }
    }
    // ...
}
```

#### Proposed Fix

Use `singleflight.Group` in `podContainerManagerImpl.Destroy()` to deduplicate concurrent calls for the same cgroup. This ensures only one D-Bus `StopUnit` call proceeds per cgroup while other callers wait and receive the same result, avoiding the channel overwrite race entirely.

### Environment

- Kubernetes version: v1.34+
- CRI: CRI-O (crun/runc)
- cgroup driver: systemd

/kind bug
/sig node
/area kubelet

title: genfeaturegates: Add linkCode and linkKEPs to json output for consistency with markdown
body:
### What would you like to be added?

The recently added [genfeaturegates tool](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/genfeaturegates/genfeaturegates.go) outputs feature gate information in both Markdown and json formats. However, I noticed that the json output is missing `linkCode` and `linkKEPs` fields that are present in the markdown output.

Markdown output includes:
- `[code](https://cs.k8s.io/?q=...&repos=kubernetes/kubernetes)`
- `[KEPs](https://cs.k8s.io/?q=...&repos=kubernetes/enhancements)`

JSON output currently lacks these links.

### Why is this needed?

I'm working on k/docs (kubernetes/website) and discovered this inconsistency.
Having consistent output between formats would help tools and documentation that consume the json output.

### Proposal

Unless there is a specific reason for omitting these fields from json, I would like to add `linkCode` and `linkKEPs` fields to match what's already in the Markdown output.

title: Preemption logic does not consider pod criticality
body:
### What happened?

Preemption logic `evictPodsToFreeRequests` and its helpers do not consider priority of the preemptable pods between them, when deciding which one to preempt.

The function `getPodsToPreempt` buckets pods by QoS (BestEffort, Burstable, Guaranteed), but fails to sort or prioritize them by `PodPriority` within those buckets. Please refer to:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4cf195304caa519be476b367267f6c656bce19f7/pkg/kubelet/preemption/preemption.go#L94C1-L191C2

When having a preemptor pod with the highest priority, a `BestEffort` critical pod (with lower priority than the preemptor) will be preempted first, than a `Burstable` pod with low priority.


### What did you expect to happen?

* Priority should be considered to determine which pods to preempt first, not only the quality of service, thus making possible to preempt first a `Burstable` pod with low priority, than a `BestEffort` critical pod.
* The `admitPod` causing the preemption should be logged to communicate which pod's admission is causing the mechanism to trigger.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Deploy any pod with `system-node-critical` priority that requires more resources than the current available, while having a running `BestEffort` pod with `system-cluster-critical` priority and a `Burstable` pod with low priority, to trigger the preemption mechanism.

After downloading kubectl 1.35.0, I attempted to verify the cosign keyless signature. This failed for amd64 but succeeds for arm64.

```bash
    --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \

# arm64
cosign verify-blob https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/arm64/kubectl \
    --signature https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/arm64/kubectl.sig \

    --certificate-identity krel-staging@k8s-releng-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

### What did you expect to happen?

The command should have printed:

```plaintext
Verified OK
```

But the error message was:


title: ci-kubernetes-unit-dependencies failing due to otelgrpc v0.64.0 nil pointer panic
body:
### What happened?

The `ci-kubernetes-unit-dependencies` CI job is failing after updating `go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/instrumentation/google.golang.org/grpc/otelgrpc` from v0.60.0 to v0.64.0.

**Failed job**: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-unit-dependencies/2002001097211777024

### Root Cause

Commit [07504e453](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/commit/07504e45307f41b8b4e609324a3b62374ad6008f) in otelgrpc removed nil checks from `WithTracerProvider` and `WithMeterProvider` options. When Kubernetes passes a nil `TracerProvider` in `staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/storagebackend/factory/etcd3.go:326`:

```go
otelgrpc.WithTracerProvider(c.TracerProvider),  // c.TracerProvider can be nil
```

The nil now overwrites the default global provider, causing a panic in `NewClientHandler()` when it calls `c.TracerProvider.Tracer(...)`.

/kind bug
/priority important-soon

title: v1.35.0 Prefilght Check logic for cgroup version vs kubelet version
body:
### What would you like to be added?

I did try the upgrade, but failed on 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.35.md#no-really-you-must-read-this-before-you-upgrade because of `the SystemVerification preflight check throws an error if cgroups v1 is detected and the detected kubelet version is v1.35 or newer. For older versions of kubelet, a preflight warning is displayed.`
I'm used to set `--ignore-preflight-errors=KubeletVersion` because my kubelet is containerized so 'kubelet --version' can't be run and make the whole `SystemVerification` check to fail

My suggestion would be to check cgroups version, and KubeletVersion only if cgroup=V1 because setting `--ignore-preflight-errors=SystemVerification` will certainly work but I could miss some basic checks


### Why is this needed?

The `if cgroup version is 2 then it's ok` logic would prevent the full `SystemVerification` preflight check to fail if kubelet version can't be checked

title: APIService remains unhealthy due to kube-apiserver reusing connection to incorrect endpoint and not verifying server certificate
body:
### What happened?

When kube-apiserver is deployed on a new control-plane node before kube-proxy is running, the AvailableConditionController, which checks the availability of registered APIServices, may connect to the Service’s ClusterIP before it is proxied by kube-proxy. As a result, the connection can be routed to an external server that happens to be listening on the same IP, causing the APIService to be reported as unhealthy due to unexpected responses.

However, even after the kube-proxy runs and proxys the ClusterIP, because of transport-layer connection caching and the fact that kube-apiserver is hard-coded to skip server certificate validation (even when the APIService’s `insecureSkipTLSVerify` is set to false), the APIService can remain unhealthy until the kube-apiserver is restarted:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5151f58ef08d9fb26931019d6d844292aeb57637/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/controllers/status/remote/remote_available_controller.go#L179-L184



### What did you expect to happen?

kube-apiserver should be able to recover from corner cases where it mistakenly establishes a connection to an incorrect server that never returns the expected response during APIService availability checks. It can be addressed either by verifying the server’s certificate when the APIService’s caBundle is provided, or by avoiding reuse of cached connections when the server returns an unexpected response.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Install an APIService with a caBundle configured and backed by a ClusterIP Service.
2. Run an HTTPS API server outside the cluster that listens to the ClusterIP and is routable from the cluster and returns 404 for unknown paths.
3. Add a new control-plane node where kube-apiserver starts before kube-proxy is scheduled on the node.
4. Check the kube-apiserver logs: the APIService continues to be reported as unhealthy due to 404 status code even after kube-proxy is running on the node.

title: Kubelet cannot handle multiple ResourceClaims if one is already prepared
body:
### What happened?

When using Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) with ResourceClaims, kubelet fails with:

    Error: internal error: unable to get claim info for ResourceClaim <name>

The error occurs when:
1. A first pod is created that references a single ResourceClaim.
2. A second pod is created that references the same ResourceClaim plus an additional one.

The failure happens during container creation, after scheduling succeeded.

The issue is reproducible using the dra-example-driver from kubernetes-sigs.

Potential spots where log may occurs:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.34/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/manager.go#L417
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.34/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/manager.go#L442
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.34/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/manager.go#L498

### What did you expect to happen?

The second pod should successfully start with both ResourceClaims prepared.

Notably, the same set of ResourceClaims works correctly when requested in the opposite order:
- When the first pod uses both ResourceClaims, and the second pod uses only one - Works ✅ 
- When the first pod uses one ResourceClaim, and the second pod then uses both - Not working 🔴 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Deploy the dra-example-driver:
   https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-example-driver

2. Create two ResourceClaims:
```yaml
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceClaim
metadata:
  name: first-resource-claim
spec:
  devices:
    requests:
    - name: request
      exactly:
        deviceClassName: gpu.example.com
        allocationMode: ExactCount
        count: 1
---
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceClaim
metadata:
  name: second-resource-claim
spec:
  devices:
    requests:
    - name: request
      exactly:
        deviceClassName: gpu.example.com
        allocationMode: ExactCount
        count: 1
```

3. Create a first pod that references only the first ResourceClaim:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test-pod-1
spec:
  containers:
  - name: container
    image: busybox
    command: ["sleep", "infinity"]
    resources:
      claims:
      - name: first
  resourceClaims:
  - name: first
    resourceClaimName: first-resource-claim
  restartPolicy: Never
```

4. Wait until the pod is running.
5. Create a second pod that references both ResourceClaims:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test-pod-2
spec:
  containers:
  - name: container
    image: busybox
    command: ["sleep", "infinity"]
    resources:
      claims:
      - name: first
      - name: second
  resourceClaims:
  - name: first
    resourceClaimName: first-resource-claim
  - name: second
    resourceClaimName: second-resource-claim
  restartPolicy: Never
```

title: Before mount the volume, kubelet cannot determine whether CSI is registered.
body:
### What happened?

During the process of attaching volumes by kubelet, if the CSI plugin is not registered, it will only be known whether the CSI plugin is registered when the kubelet actually calls the CSI's volume mount method (SetUp). If the CSI plugin is not registered and there are too many volumes to mount, this can cause the kubelet CPU usage to spike in a short period of time.
Should we check whether the CSI plugin is registered before mounting the volume? This could reduce unnecessary coroutine creation and lower CPU usage.
The CSI plugin is only checked for existence when the SetUpAt method is called.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2a3a6605ac9b184711ef212ecbe26c8af4a8bac8/pkg/volume/csi/csi_mounter.go#L102-L110
### What did you expect to happen?

After kubelet knows whether CSI is registered, it proceeds with volume mounting.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

A node has multiple pods, and there are a large number of volumes that need to be mounted by CSI. However, the CSI plugin is not registered.

```go
2025-12-17T02:12:17.884482085Z 
```

### What did you expect to happen?

The getEventKey function should handle nil fields gracefully instead of panicking. It should either:
  1. Check for nil before accessing nested fields and use empty strings as defaults
  2. Return an error that can be handled by the caller
  3. Skip events with incomplete data

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

  This occurred in an OpenShift environment during operator installation/reconciliation. The logs before the panic show:
  - Multiple "resource name may not be empty" errors from the OperatorCondition controller
  - Conflict errors when updating Operator status
  - Rapid CSV reconciliation for servicemeshoperator3.v3.2.0 and kiali-operator.v2.17.2

  The panic happened in the event broadcaster goroutine, which runs independently from the main reconciliation loops.

### Anything else we need to know?

  The getEventKey function in events_cache.go constructs an event key by joining multiple fields:
```go
  The `getEventKey` function in `events_cache.go` constructs an event key by joining multiple fields:

  func getEventKey(event *v1.Event) string {
      return strings.Join([]string{
          event.Source.Component,      // panics if event is nil
          event.Source.Host,
          // ...
      }, "")
  }
```
  If `event` (which is a pointer `*v1.Event`) is nil, accessing `event.Source` causes
  a nil pointer dereference. The function lacks a nil check for the `event` parameter
  before accessing its fields.

title: globalmount path may be residual while pod creation-deletion
body:
### What happened?

1. created a pod A
2. pod A starting `mountDevice` , but at this time, the csi-plugin pod was upgrading, kubelet received `rpc error: code = Unavailable error reading from server: EOF`, marked the volume device  `uncertain`, actually the globalmount was mounted.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/15673d04e30c711a7bb0f0efe6abf4baead1463b/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L690-L694
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/15673d04e30c711a7bb0f0efe6abf4baead1463b/pkg/volume/csi/csi_client.go#L449-L451
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/15673d04e30c711a7bb0f0efe6abf4baead1463b/pkg/volume/csi/csi_client.go#L711-L728
3. kubelet retried to mountDevice for pod A, but at this time. the csi-plugin pod was terminated and had not started again, the kubelet received `rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial unix xxx/csi.sock: connect: connection refused`, it was not a `UncertainProgressError` and then marked the volume device  `unmounted`. Actually it failed at `csi.NodeSupportsStageUnstage(ctx)` this time, hadn't called `csi.NodeStageVolume` yet.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/15673d04e30c711a7bb0f0efe6abf4baead1463b/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L674-L683
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/15673d04e30c711a7bb0f0efe6abf4baead1463b/pkg/volume/csi/csi_client.go#L704-L706
4. pod A was deleted, but the volume device in asw was unmounted, kubelet didn't call umountDevice, then the globalmount was residual.


I think that while a volume was uncertain, kubelet retried to mount it again, althrough kubelet may received a not `UncertainProgressError`, we should not change it's status to unmounted, it should be always uncertain until called unmountDevice successfully

### What did you expect to happen?

globalmount can be unmounted under any circumstances

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

above
