title: [Flaking test] [sig-autoscaling] [Feature:HPA] "Should scale with a CRD targetRef": conflict updating the custom resource in GetReplicas is fatal
body:
### Which jobs are flaking?

All four upstream jobs that run `[Feature:HPA]`:

- `ci-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu`, `ci-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu-alpha-beta` (daily periodics, testgrid `sig-autoscaling-hpa-periodics`)
- `pull-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu`, `pull-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu-alpha-beta` (presubmits, currently `optional: true`)

Scanning `junit_01.xml` of every retained build in `gs://kubernetes-ci-logs` (2026-06-10 to 2026-09-14, 397 builds, 42 excluded because they produced no junit):

| Job | Runs | Failures of this test | Rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `ci-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu` | 95 | 2 | 2.1% |
| `ci-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu-alpha-beta` | 97 | 1 | 1.0% |
| `pull-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu` | 84 | 7 | 8.3% |
| `pull-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu-alpha-beta` | 79 | 3 | 3.8% |
| **Total** | **355** | **13** | **3.7%** |

All 13 failures are the same 409 conflict described below; the test has no other failure mode upstream in that window. The 10 presubmit hits span 8 distinct PRs (#139142 alone hit it three times). Testgrid retains only the last 15 runs for these tabs and triage covers 14 days, so both usually show green at a daily cadence and this rate.

Examples:

- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu/2082774494639820800
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu/2084949925476438016
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu-alpha-beta/2082026302444933120
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/pr-logs/pull/139142/pull-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu/2065593706815164416
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/pr-logs/pull/140536/pull-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu-alpha-beta/2077464184747986944

Also seen downstream in OpenShift CI, which runs this test unmodified as part of the `[Suite:k8s]` conformance suite: ~0.4–0.8% of runs on OpenShift 4.20 (Kubernetes 1.33), tracked as https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-63224.

### Which tests are flaking?

```
[sig-autoscaling] [Feature:HPA] Horizontal pod autoscaling (scale resource: CPU) CustomResourceDefinition Should scale with a CRD targetRef
```

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/153454f8018f6c3e1e6da09eec607f2666aa7802/test/e2e/autoscaling/horizontal_pod_autoscaling.go#L147

### Since when has it been flaking?

Continuously across the full retention window of the logs bucket (June 2026 onward; failures dated June through September 2026), and latent since the test was added in #112335 (Sep 2022, v1.26). The race has always been fatal: before #121916 (Nov 2023, v1.29) moved the polling onto `framework.HandleRetry`, the same `Update` error hit `framework.ExpectNoError`. That refactor only changed how the failure is reported.

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-autoscaling-hpa-periodics#gce-cos-autoscaling-hpa-cpu (only the last 15 runs are retained; see the prow links above for the failures)

### Reason for failure (if possible)

Failure output:

```
[FAILED] timeout waiting 15m0s for 2 replicas: Told to stop trying after 60.095s.
Unexpected final error while getting int: Operation cannot be fulfilled on testcrds.autoscalinge2e.example.com "foo-crd": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again
At one point, however, the function did return successfully.
Yet, Eventually failed because the matcher was not satisfied:
Expected
    <int>: 1
to equal
    <int>: 2
In [It] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/autoscaling/horizontal_pod_autoscaling.go:241
```

Note "stop trying after 60s" against a 15m budget: this is not a real timeout. The poll aborts on the first conflict, roughly 14 minutes early.

Mechanics:

1. The CRD under test has a scale subresource but no status subresource:
   https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/153454f8018f6c3e1e6da09eec607f2666aa7802/test/e2e/framework/autoscaling/autoscaling_utils.go#L1387-L1394
   Nothing reconciles it, so the test stands in for a controller: every poll of `ResourceConsumer.GetReplicas` mirrors the child Deployment's `readyReplicas` into the CR's `status.replicas` with a full read-modify-write (`Get` -> `SetNestedField` -> `Update`) on the main resource:
   https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/153454f8018f6c3e1e6da09eec607f2666aa7802/test/e2e/framework/autoscaling/autoscaling_utils.go#L722-L746

2. Meanwhile the HPA controller writes `spec.replicas` to the same object through `/scale` on its own 15s sync period. When that lands between the `Get` and the `Update`, the `Update` carries a stale `resourceVersion` and the API server returns 409 Conflict.

3. `WaitForReplicas` polls `GetReplicas` through `framework.HandleRetry`:
   https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/153454f8018f6c3e1e6da09eec607f2666aa7802/test/e2e/framework/autoscaling/autoscaling_utils.go#L758-L766
   `framework.ShouldRetry` only treats timeouts, 429, 503, `io.EOF` and explicitly marked transient errors as retryable. A 409 is not on the list, so `HandleRetry` wraps it in `gomega.StopTrying` and `Eventually` gives up immediately:
   https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/153454f8018f6c3e1e6da09eec607f2666aa7802/test/e2e/framework/get.go#L70-L113

The window is a couple of round trips wide per poll, polled every 20s, against a writer firing every 15s, which matches the observed low-single-digit-percent rate.

The conflict reproduces deterministically outside the e2e with the same CRD shape: GET the CR, write `spec.replicas` via `/scale` (what the HPA does), then PUT the stale object back. It fails with the exact error above.

### Anything else we need to know?

Prior attempt: #134664 added `apierrors.IsConflict` to `framework.ShouldRetry` (+1 line in `test/e2e/framework/get.go`). It received no review, sig-autoscaling asked for sig-testing input, and it was closed by the lifecycle bot in April 2026. It had no tracking issue, hence this one.

Proposed fix (PR to follow): keep the change local to `GetReplicas` and replace the `Get`/`Update` pair with a JSON merge patch of only `status.replicas` on the main resource. A merge patch carries no `resourceVersion`, so it cannot collide with the HPA's `/scale` write, and it stops writing `spec.replicas` (the HPA's field) back at all. It also drops one API call per poll. Verified against a live cluster: the patch succeeds after a concurrent `/scale` write, `/scale` then reports the HPA's `spec.replicas` untouched, `status.replicas` updated and `status.selector` intact, and 50 interleaved `/scale`-vs-patch writes produced zero failures.

Alternatives considered:

- `retry.RetryOnConflict` around the read-modify-write: works, but tolerates the race rather than removing it, and keeps rewriting `spec.replicas`.
- Add a status subresource and use `UpdateStatus`: still a read-modify-write on the same `resourceVersion`, so it still needs conflict handling.
- #134664's approach (retry 409 in `ShouldRetry`): fixes this too, but changes semantics for every `HandleRetry` caller, and the next poll would only come 20s later.

Both HPA presubmits carry `# TODO: set optional: false once tests not flaky` in test-infra. This is currently the only thing failing this test, so fixing it is a prerequisite for making them required.

title: Start localhost nodeport proxy only when nodeport address contains 127.0.0.1
body:
The nftables localhost nodeport (https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/6032) proxy always runs on 127.0.0.1, however it starts even if someone only writes `--nodeport-addresses.=127.0.0.2/32`. This doesn't quite make sense since we're running the proxy on an IP that was not specified.

It's unlikely a user runs into this, but I think we should change this for logics sake. The rule would be to start the proxy when `127.0.0.1` is included in the loopback address, so `127.0.0.1/32` or `127.0.0.0/8` would start the proxy, but `127.0.0.2/32` would not.

title: Job controller does not recover when a Job is deleted and recreated with the same name during status tracking
body:
### What happened?

When a Job is deleted and immediately recreated with the **same name**, the job controller in
kube-controller-manager can get stuck on the old Job and never manage the new one.

The new Job stays empty forever — no pods are created:

```
$ kubectl -n kube-system get job helm-install-harvester-cloud-provider
NAME                                   STATUS    COMPLETIONS   DURATION   AGE
helm-install-harvester-cloud-provider  Running   0/1           18m        18m
```

`0 Active (0 Ready) / 0 Succeeded / 0 Failed`.

kube-controller-manager logs this error:

```
E0319 21:58:00.617079       1 job_controller.go:659] "Unhandled Error" err="syncing job: tracking status: adding uncounted pods to status: Operation cannot be fulfilled on jobs.batch \"helm-install-harvester-cloud-provider\": StorageError: invalid object, Code: 4, Key: /registry/jobs/kube-system/helm-install-harvester-cloud-provider, ResourceVersion: 0, AdditionalErrorMsg: Precondition failed: UID in precondition: 6ae0b0b2-34c6-42e2-afc9-d7616ec93f2e, UID in object meta: 8515b052-3a07-43e8-bf01-d898e2b9c27c" logger="UnhandledError"
```

In simple words:

1. The job controller starts syncing Job "X" and reads it, including its UID.
2. While that sync is running, something deletes Job "X" and creates a new Job with the same
   name but a **different UID**.
3. The controller finishes the sync and tries to write the status of the Job it read.
4. The API server rejects the write, because the UID it was given no longer matches the UID
   of the object stored under that name.
5. From this point on the new Job is not driven forward, and no pods are ever created for it.

The two UIDs in the error message are the old Job (`UID in precondition`) and the new Job
(`UID in object meta`), which is what makes this a delete-and-recreate race.

### What did you expect to happen?

When the job controller finds that the Job it was working on has been replaced by a different
Job with the same name, it should:

- Discard the stale in-progress work for the old UID, and
- Start managing the new Job normally, so that its pods are created.

A Job that is deleted and recreated with the same name should end up running, not stuck at
zero pods.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This is a timing-dependent race, so it does not reproduce every time. It needs the delete and
the recreate to land while a status sync for the old Job is in flight.

**Synthetic reproduction** — repeatedly replace a Job with the same name, on a busy cluster:

```bash
kubectl create ns jobrace

for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  kubectl -n jobrace delete job racer --ignore-not-found --wait=false
  kubectl -n jobrace create job racer --image=busybox -- /bin/sh -c 'sleep 5'
  sleep 0.2
done

# then watch for a Job that never gets a pod
kubectl -n jobrace get job racer -o wide
kubectl -n jobrace get pods
```

Then check the kube-controller-manager log for `UID in precondition`:

```bash
kubectl -n kube-system logs -l component=kube-controller-manager --tail=-1 \
  | grep -i "UID in precondition"
```

**Real-world reproduction** — this is how we hit it. On RKE2/Harvester, `helm-controller`
deletes and recreates its `helm-install-*` Job when the chart's configuration changes. During
cluster provisioning, when the cluster is under load, the delete and recreate happen very close
together and the install Job gets stuck, which blocks provisioning:

1. Install Harvester v1.8.0.
2. Install Rancher Manager v2.14.1.
3. Import Harvester into Rancher Manager.
4. Provision an RKE2 guest cluster.
5. Provisioning frequently hangs, with `job helm-install-harvester-cloud-provider` showing
   `0 Active (0 Ready) / 0 Succeeded / 0 Failed`.

Downstream reports with full logs:

- https://github.com/k3s-io/helm-controller/issues/311
- https://github.com/rancher/rke2/issues/9996
- https://github.com/rancher/rke2/issues/8357
- https://github.com/harvester/harvester/issues/10188


### Anything else we need to know?

**Why we are reporting this here.** This was first raised against `helm-controller`. The
maintainer's assessment was that the delete-and-recreate handling is an upstream Kubernetes
issue rather than something that can be fixed downstream:

> Kube-controller-manager KEP-2307 job tracking with finalizers does not properly handle
> recreation of jobs under high load. If the job is deleted and recreated while pod counting
> is in progress, it will fail to patch the job status, and won't reenqueue the job for
> processing again until it is modified. This is an upstream Kubernetes bug, not something we
> can fix here.
> — https://github.com/k3s-io/helm-controller/issues/311#issuecomment-4100147480

Asked again in September 2026 whether recent downstream changes had resolved it, the answer was:

> There is no guarantee that this is fixed until the bug is resolved upstream, but
> https://github.com/k3s-io/helm-controller/pull/353 will definitely cover some gaps in job
> recreation when multiple resources that trigger job updates fire within the same sync interval.
> — https://github.com/k3s-io/helm-controller/issues/311#issuecomment-5606714470

So PR #353 is a mitigation that reduces how often the race is triggered, not a fix for the
behaviour described here.

title: MutatingAdmissionPolicy: a JSON patch value holding an Object initializer inside a list panics the apiserver
body:
## What happened?

A `MutatingAdmissionPolicy` JSON patch whose `value` is a **list containing an `Object` initializer** panics during patch evaluation:

```
panic: reflect.Set: value of type *structpb.Struct is not assignable to type *structpb.Value
```

The panic is not recovered inside the patch code, so it propagates out of admission evaluation.

The cause is a type contract violation in `(*ObjectVal).ConvertToNative`, `staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/cel/mutation/dynamic/objects.go`:

```go
if typeDesc == reflect.TypeOf(&structpb.Value{}) {
    return structpb.NewStruct(result)
}
```

Asked for a `*structpb.Value`, it returns a `*structpb.Struct`.

For a bare object this is harmless in practice, because the only caller, `evaluatePatchExpression` in `pkg/admission/plugin/policy/mutating/patch/json_patch.go`, marshals the result to JSON immediately and both types encode identically. So the wrong type is never observed.

Inside a list it is not harmless. cel-go's `baseList.ConvertToNative` takes the `JSONValueType` branch, recurses as `[]*structpb.Value`, and then assigns each converted element by reflection:

```go
nativeList.Index(i).Set(reflect.ValueOf(nativeElemVal))
```

`reflect` enforces the element type there, and the mismatch becomes a panic.

## What did you expect to happen?

The patch to apply, producing a list of objects at the given path. There is nothing invalid about the expression, and the equivalent patch with a bare `Object` initializer works.

## How can we reproduce it?

Two cases added to the existing `TestJSONPatch` table in `pkg/admission/plugin/policy/mutating/patch/json_patch_test.go`. The first panics, the second passes.

```go
{
	name: "jsonPatch value is a list holding an Object initializer",
	expression: `[
				JSONPatch{
					op: "add",
					path: "/spec/template/spec/tolerations",
					value: [
						Object.spec.template.spec.tolerations{key: "example", operator: "Exists", effect: "NoSchedule"}
					]
				},
			]`,
	gvr:    deploymentGVR,
	object: &appsv1.Deployment{Spec: appsv1.DeploymentSpec{Replicas: ptr.To[int32](1)}},
	expectedResult: &appsv1.Deployment{Spec: appsv1.DeploymentSpec{
		Replicas: ptr.To[int32](1),
		Template: corev1.PodTemplateSpec{Spec: corev1.PodSpec{Tolerations: []corev1.Toleration{{
			Key:      "example",
			Operator: corev1.TolerationOpExists,
			Effect:   corev1.TaintEffectNoSchedule,
		}}}},
	}},
},
{
	name: "jsonPatch value is a bare Object initializer",
	expression: `[
				JSONPatch{
					op: "add",
					path: "/spec/template/spec/securityContext",
					value: Object.spec.template.spec.securityContext{runAsNonRoot: true}
				},
			]`,
	gvr:    deploymentGVR,
	object: &appsv1.Deployment{Spec: appsv1.DeploymentSpec{Replicas: ptr.To[int32](1)}},
	expectedResult: &appsv1.Deployment{Spec: appsv1.DeploymentSpec{
		Replicas: ptr.To[int32](1),
		Template: corev1.PodTemplateSpec{Spec: corev1.PodSpec{
			SecurityContext: &corev1.PodSecurityContext{RunAsNonRoot: ptr.To(true)},
		}},
	}},
},
```

Result:

```
=== RUN   TestJSONPatch/jsonPatch_value_is_a_list_holding_an_Object_initializer
panic: reflect.Set: value of type *structpb.Struct is not assignable to type *structpb.Value
FAIL	k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/policy/mutating/patch

=== RUN   TestJSONPatch/jsonPatch_value_is_a_bare_Object_initializer
--- PASS: TestJSONPatch/jsonPatch_value_is_a_bare_Object_initializer
ok  	k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/policy/mutating/patch
```

Because the panic aborts the test binary, the two cases have to be run separately to see the control pass.

## Anything else we need to know?

`structpb.NewValue(result)` in place of `structpb.NewStruct(result)` returns the requested type and is the obvious candidate, but the conversion contract is sig-api-machinery's call, so this is an issue and not a PR. Happy to send the fix and the two test cases if that is welcome.

This reproduces against `k8s.io/apiserver` v0.36.4, which resolves cel-go v0.26.0. The same defect reaches Kyverno, whose MutatingPolicy JSON patch code is a fork of `json_patch.go` carrying the identical line, and there it reproduces with cel-go v0.31.0. So it is not specific to one cel-go release. Kyverno tracks it as kyverno/kyverno#17611, reported by a user hitting it on a live cluster, where the unrecovered panic took down their reports controller and their mutating webhook.

## Kubernetes version

`k8s.io/apiserver` v0.36.4

## Cloud provider

Not applicable, reproduced from the apiserver unit tests.

/sig api-machinery
/area admission-control

title: kubectl describe pod does not show env vars sourced from valueFrom.fileKeyRef
body:
### What happened?

`kubectl describe pod` prints nothing for a container env var whose source is `valueFrom.fileKeyRef` (KEP-3721 / `EnvFiles`, beta and on by default since v1.35, GA on master). The variable does not appear under `Environment:` at all, not even its name. Env vars with a plain `value`, or with `configMapKeyRef`, `secretKeyRef`, `fieldRef` and `resourceFieldRef`, are printed as usual.

Cause: `describeContainerEnvVars` switches over the `EnvVarSource` kinds it knows about and has no case for `FileKeyRef` (and no `default`), so the entry is silently skipped:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go#L1990-L2013

### What did you expect to happen?

The variable to be listed in the same style as the other key references, for example:

```
    Environment:
      PLAIN:  1
      TOKEN:  <set to the key 'TOKEN' of file 'app.env' in volume 'config'>  Optional: false
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: envfile
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  initContainers:
  - name: writer
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo TOKEN=abc > /data/app.env"]
    volumeMounts:
    - name: config
      mountPath: /data
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "env; sleep 3600"]
    env:
    - name: PLAIN
      value: "1"
    - name: TOKEN
      valueFrom:
        fileKeyRef:
          volumeName: config
          path: app.env
          key: TOKEN
    volumeMounts:
    - name: config
      mountPath: /data
  volumes:
  - name: config
    emptyDir: {}
```

```console
$ kubectl apply -f pod.yaml
$ kubectl describe pod envfile | grep -A2 'Environment:'
    Environment:
      PLAIN:  1
    Mounts:
```

`TOKEN` is missing, although `kubectl exec envfile -- env` shows `TOKEN=abc`.

At the unit level, calling `describeContainerEnvVars` with a container whose only env var has `ValueFrom.FileKeyRef` set produces just the `Environment:` header. A regression test that fails against the `v1.37.0` tag is in the linked PR.

### Anything else we need to know?

Someone debugging an env-file-backed pod can easily conclude from `describe` that the variable is not set. The fix is a one-case addition to the switch; PR to follow.

title: kubectl describe service prints "+ 0 more..." when 3 ready endpoints are followed by not-ready endpoints
body:
### What happened?

For a Service whose EndpointSlices contain exactly three ready endpoints followed by one or more not-ready endpoints, `kubectl describe service` prints:

```
Endpoints:                10.0.0.1:80,10.0.0.2:80,10.0.0.3:80 + 0 more...
```

Cause: `formatEndpointSlices` sets its `more` flag as soon as it visits a fourth endpoint, but that check runs before the readiness filter, while only ready endpoints are counted. A not-ready fourth endpoint flips the flag without being counted, so the suffix reports `count - max = 0`. Both the ported branch and the headless (no ports) branch have the same ordering:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go#L5266-L5281
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go#L5289-L5307

The check was correct before the readiness filter was added in #126932 (v1.32), because every visited endpoint was also counted.

### What did you expect to happen?

```
Endpoints:                10.0.0.1:80,10.0.0.2:80,10.0.0.3:80
```

and `+ N more...` only when there are more than three ready endpoints.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a Service with four backing pods where exactly one is not ready (for example a Deployment with `replicas: 4` and a readiness probe, then break the probe in one pod), and run `kubectl describe service <name>`.

Directly, with a hand-made EndpointSlice:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
---
apiVersion: discovery.k8s.io/v1
kind: EndpointSlice
metadata:
  name: web-abcde
  labels:
    kubernetes.io/service-name: web
addressType: IPv4
ports:
- name: http
  port: 80
endpoints:
- addresses: ["10.0.0.1"]
  conditions: {ready: true}
- addresses: ["10.0.0.2"]
  conditions: {ready: true}
- addresses: ["10.0.0.3"]
  conditions: {ready: true}
- addresses: ["10.0.0.4"]
  conditions: {ready: false}
```

```console
$ kubectl apply -f svc.yaml
$ kubectl describe service web | grep Endpoints
Endpoints:                10.0.0.1:80,10.0.0.2:80,10.0.0.3:80 + 0 more...
```

At the unit level, `formatEndpointSlices` with three ready and one not-ready endpoint returns `"10.0.0.1:80,10.0.0.2:80,10.0.0.3:80 + 0 more..."`; a regression test that fails against the `v1.37.0` tag is in the linked PR.

### Anything else we need to know?

The output is misleading rather than harmful, but it is the kind of thing people paste into incident reports. The fix is to derive the suffix from the ready count after filtering; PR to follow.

/sig cli

title: kubectl describe node: per-pod resource rows print -9223372036854775808% on nodes without allocatable and disagree with the totals during in-place resize
body:
### What happened?

Two related defects in the "Non-terminated Pods" table printed by `kubectl describe node` (`describeNodeResource`), both absent from the "Allocated resources" totals printed right below it:

**1. Garbage percentages when the node has no allocatable resources.**
On a node with no `status.capacity` / `status.allocatable` (kubelet has not posted status yet, a Node object created by hand, some virtual nodes), every pod row prints:

```
Non-terminated Pods:          (1 in total)
  Namespace   Name    CPU Requests                  CPU Limits                    Memory Requests                Memory Limits                  Age
  ---------   ----    ------------                  ----------                    ---------------                -------------                  ---
  default     pod-1   100m (-9223372036854775808%)  200m (-9223372036854775808%)  100Mi (-9223372036854775808%)  200Mi (-9223372036854775808%)  5m
Allocated resources:
  (Total limits may be over 100 percent, i.e., overcommitted.)
  Resource           Requests   Limits
  --------           --------   ------
  cpu                100m (0%)  200m (0%)
  memory             100Mi (0%) 200Mi (0%)
```

The per-pod percentages divide by allocatable with no zero guard (`x/0` gives `+Inf`/`NaN`, and `int64(...)` of that prints the minimum int64):
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go#L4066-L4076
The totals guard the very same division and print `0%`:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go#L4085-L4098

**2. Rows and totals disagree while a pod is being resized in place.**
Since 97f00d18eeb (#137683) the per-pod rows are computed with `UseStatusResources: true` (the resources actually allocated to the containers), but `getPodsTotalRequestsAndLimits` still uses the pod spec only:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go#L4141-L4145
While a pod's `status.containerStatuses[].resources` differ from its spec (in-place resize in progress, or an infeasible resize), a row can show `500m (50%)` while the totals for the same node show `100m (10%)`, and the rows no longer add up to the totals.

### What did you expect to happen?

1. Rows print `0%` when allocatable is zero, exactly like the totals do.
2. Rows and totals use the same resource accounting so that the rows always sum to the totals.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

For (1):

```console
$ kubectl create -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Node
metadata:
  name: empty-node
EOF
$ kubectl run pod-1 --image=busybox --overrides='{"spec":{"nodeName":"empty-node"}}' --requests=cpu=100m,memory=100Mi --limits=cpu=200m,memory=200Mi -- sleep 3600
$ kubectl describe node empty-node | grep -A4 'Non-terminated Pods'
```

For (2), with the `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` feature, resize a running pod's CPU request (for example `kubectl patch pod pod-1 --subresource resize -p '{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"pod-1","resources":{"requests":{"cpu":"500m"}}}]}}'`) and describe the node while `status.containerStatuses[0].resources` differ from the spec.

At the unit level, calling `describeNodeResource` with a Node that has no status prints the `-9223372036854775808%` rows above, and with a pod whose container status reports 500m while the spec says 100m the row prints `500m (50%)` and the totals `100m (10%)`. Regression tests for both cases that fail against the `v1.37.0` tag are in the linked PR.

### Anything else we need to know?

(1) is long-standing (the per-pod loop has been unguarded since it was introduced). (2) was introduced when the rows switched to status resources without the totals following. PR to follow; it guards the per-pod division the way the totals already do and uses the same `PodResourcesOptions` for both.

/kind bug
/sig cli

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.37.0
```

Reproduced with unit tests against the `v1.37.0` tag; the code is unchanged on master at bc32e8eb00f.

title: ParseToLabelSelector rejects "!=", so kubectl create pdb and kubectl set selector fail on selectors that work with kubectl get -l
body:
### What happened?

`metav1.ParseToLabelSelector` rejects the `!=` operator, so the kubectl commands that build a `LabelSelector` from a user-supplied selector string fail on a selector that works everywhere else:

```console
$ kubectl create pdb web-pdb --selector='app!=web' --min-available=1
error: "!=" is not a valid label selector operator

$ kubectl set selector service web 'app!=web'
error: "!=" is not a valid label selector operator

$ kubectl get pods -l 'app!=web'     # works
```

`labels.Parse` accepts `key!=value`, but `ParseToLabelSelector`, whose comment says it "should be kept in sync with the parser in pkg/labels/selector.go", has no case for `selection.NotEquals` and falls through to the default error (only `>` / `<` are rejected deliberately):
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/helpers.go#L117-L144

`key!=value` selects exactly the objects that `key notin (value)` selects (`labels.Requirement.Matches` treats both as "key absent, or value not in the set"), so it can be represented losslessly as `LabelSelectorOpNotIn` with a single value. The reverse direction, `LabelSelectorAsSelector`, already turns `NotIn` back into a selector with the same semantics.

Callers in kubectl: `kubectl create pdb` (`create_pdb.go`) and `kubectl set selector` (`set_selector.go`).

### What did you expect to happen?

The selector is accepted and produces:

```yaml
selector:
  matchExpressions:
  - key: app
    operator: NotIn
    values: ["web"]
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run either command above against any cluster, or call `metav1.ParseToLabelSelector("foo!=bar")`. A regression test that fails against the `v1.37.0` tag is in the linked PR; it also checks that every parsed `LabelSelector` selects the same label sets as the original selector string.

### Anything else we need to know?

Long-standing; the function has never handled `NotEquals`. PR to follow (one `case` in the switch plus tests).

/kind bug
/sig api-machinery
/sig cli

<details>

title: API Server Write Throughput: Reduce Write Allocations (1.37-1.38)
body:
### What would you like to be added?

This issue tracks reducing write-path allocations from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142223.

All desired improvements for 1.37 and 1.38 have landed.

Pod patch allocations were already reduced by ~35% in 1.37 (from ~152x down to ~98x), with ~70% of the remaining allocations on the write path (`handlers.PatchResource`) and ~30% in watch propagation. In 1.38, write-path allocations were reduced by another ~43% (down to ~57x-60x end-to-end and ~43x-47x on the write handler).

![Pod Patch Allocation Factor Across 1.37 & 1.38](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/Jefftree/c38742b0d91e69f247b197ce1cebf501/raw/41a2b2ed0eb68acc9233db37f1cae8b615462a13/retro_137_pod_write_chart.png)

Completed in 1.37:

- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139350
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139826
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139851
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139856
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139974
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140368
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141947
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142227

Completed in 1.38:

- ~2x (~1.1k allocs): Remove equality allocations along the update pipeline
  - [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142398
- ~20x (~4.6k allocs): Reduce `managedFields` and SSA field-tracking allocations during writes (including reset fields)
  - [x] https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/structured-merge-diff/pull/351
  - [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143329
  - [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142427
  - [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143011
- ~26x (~3.6k allocs): Reduce the unstructured conversion round-trip in Strategic Merge Patch (`ToUnstructured` / `FromUnstructuredWithValidation`)
  - [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142394

### Why is this needed?

`kube-apiserver` hits a Go runtime GC sweep ceiling around ~6 GB/s of allocations on large multicore nodes, limiting sustainable throughput when a 10 KB Pod patch allocates ~1 MB.

Write-path breakdown for a 10 KB Pod (`BenchmarkPatchPod` in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142227):

| Component | 1.38 Start | 1.38 Final | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Strategic Merge Patch | ~25x (~256 KB) | ~3x (~31 KB) | Top-level pruned unstructured map round-trip (`ToUnstructuredTopLevel` -> `SMP` -> `FromUnstructuredWithValidationTopLevel`) |
| `managedFields` / SSA | ~20x (~204 KB) | ~18x (~188 KB) | `FieldManager.Update` and `ValidateManagedFields` |
| `Pod` copies & conversion | ~17x (~170 KB) | ~9x (~91 KB) | `Pod` deep copies, semantic `DeepEqual`, and version conversions |
| Request, admission & framing | ~11x (~120 KB) | ~2x (~21 KB) | Handler, admission, and HTTP framing overhead |
| Validation | ~7x (~76 KB) | ~7x (~75 KB) | `ValidatePodUpdate` and `ValidateDeclaratively` |
| Protobuf serialization | ~7x (~68 KB) | ~8x (~77 KB) | Storage and response serialization |
| Total write path | ~87x (~894 KB, 15,133 allocs/op) | ~47x (~480 KB, 6,560 allocs/op) | `~43x` / `~443 KB` / `6,799 allocs/op` on `PatchPodStatus` (`~60x` / `~57x` in full integration with embedded etcd) |

/sig api-machinery
/sig scalability
/cc @serathius

title: kubelet: containerLogs returns HTTP 200 when the container is gone from the runtime
body:
### What happened?

When a container has been removed from the runtime but its Pod still exists, the kubelet /containerLogs endpoint can return HTTP 200 with the error message in the response body. kubectl logs then prints the error as if it were log output and exits 0, so clients cannot tell that the log fetch failed.

The root cause is an unconditional zero-byte Write() in GetKubeletContainerLogs, which is used to flush headers early for streaming logs. net/http commits the response as 200 on the first write, so an error found later by ContainerStatus() cannot change the status. The affected path is getContainerLogs() → GetKubeletContainerLogs() → GetContainerLogs(), with the container lookup happening after the response has already been committed.

### What did you expect to happen?

When the container no longer exists in the runtime, the kubelet should return a non-200 HTTP error before anything is written to the response. This allows kubectl logs and other clients to correctly detect that fetching the logs failed.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a pod with a long-running container:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: repro
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo hi; sleep 3600"]
```
2. Wait for the pod to become Running, then remove the container directly from the runtime without deleting the Pod:

>  Ive used kind here, hence the docker specific commands

```
docker exec <node> crictl --runtime-endpoint unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock ps -a
docker exec <node> crictl --runtime-endpoint unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock stop <container-id>
docker exec <node> crictl --runtime-endpoint unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock rm <container-id>
```
3. Fetch the logs:
```
kubectl logs repro -c c
kubectl get --raw '/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/repro/log?container=c' -v=8
```
Observed: 
```
I0920 22:04:14.035218   59244 raw.go:84] "Request Body" body=""
I0920 22:04:14.035468   59244 round_trippers.go:527] "Request" verb="GET" url="https://127.0.0.1:65257/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/repro/log?container=c" headers=<
        Accept: application/json, */*

        Cache-Control: no-cache, private
        Content-Type: text/plain
        Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 16:34:14 GMT
 > milliseconds=12
unable to retrieve container logs for containerd://afc02845d2117c9bafd00a8e5565e3f9a34d3f333a2e7638e9ea62d4e90ee1d9%                                                                                             
```

Note that we are seeing a 200 OK with error to get logs

title: kubectl create ingress panics when a rule path contains a comma
body:
### What happened?

`kubectl create ingress` panics when a `--rule` path contains a comma.
No cluster is needed; `--dry-run=client` is enough:

```console
$ kubectl create ingress ing --rule="foo.com/a,b=svc:8080" \
    --dry-run=client -o yaml
panic: runtime error: index out of range [1] with length 1

goroutine 1 [running]:
k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create.buildHTTPIngressPath(...)
	k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create_ingress.go:396 +0x168
k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create.(*CreateIngressOptions).buildIngressRules(...)
	k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create_ingress.go:368 +0xd0
k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create.(*CreateIngressOptions).buildIngressSpec(...)
	k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create_ingress.go:312 +0xcc
```

A comma is a legal URL path character (a sub-delim in RFC 3986), and
`ruleRegex` accepts it: the path group is `(?P<path>/.*)`. So the rule
passes `Validate`:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/400031d6953/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create_ingress.go#L223

The builders then discard that match and re-split the raw rule string,
treating the first comma as the start of the TLS clause.
`buildIngressRules` cuts the rule at `strings.Split(rule, ",")[0]`,
leaving `foo.com/a`, so `buildHTTPIngressPath` finds no `=` and indexes
past the end of the slice:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/400031d6953/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create_ingress.go#L365
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/400031d6953/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create_ingress.go#L396

`buildTLSRules` does the same split and reads the remainder as a TLS
clause:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/400031d6953/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create_ingress.go#L324

So validation and construction parse the same rule differently.

The panic is the loud case. A path that also carries `=` and `:` is
accepted and silently builds a different object than the one asked for:

```console
$ kubectl create ingress ing --rule="foo.com/a=b:c,d=svc:8080" \
    --dry-run=client -o yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: ing
spec:
  rules:
  - host: foo.com
    http:
      paths:
      - backend:
          service:
            name: b
            port:
              name: c
        path: /a
        pathType: Exact
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - foo.com
    secretName: svc:8080
status:
  loadBalancer: {}
```

The backend is `b:c` on path `/a` instead of `svc:8080` on
`/a=b:c,d`, and there is a TLS block with `secretName: svc:8080` that
was never requested. No error, no warning.

### What did you expect to happen?

The rule parsed the way `ruleRegex` reads it: the TLS clause is the
optional trailing `,tls[=secret]`, not the first comma anywhere in the
rule. For `foo.com/a,b=svc:8080`:

```yaml
spec:
  rules:
  - host: foo.com
    http:
      paths:
      - backend:
          service:
            name: svc
            port:
              number: 8080
        path: /a,b
        pathType: Exact
```

and no `tls` block, since `,tls` is absent.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

No cluster required. Each of these panics:

```console
$ kubectl create ingress ing --rule="foo.com/a,b=svc:8080" \
    --dry-run=client -o yaml
$ kubectl create ingress ing --rule="/path,x=svc:8080" \
    --dry-run=client -o yaml
$ kubectl create ingress ing --rule="foo.com/a,b=svc:8080,tls=s1" \
    --dry-run=client -o yaml
```

For the silent misparse:

```console
$ kubectl create ingress ing --rule="foo.com/a=b:c,d=svc:8080" \
    --dry-run=client -o yaml
```

At the unit level, adding a `TestCreateIngress` case with the rule
`foo.com/a,b=svc:8080` panics against master.

### Anything else we need to know?

Long-standing: the double parse dates from the original
`create ingress` implementation, and the code is unchanged on master
at 400031d6953.

A PR follows that matches each rule once with the compiled `ruleRegex`
and builds the spec from its named groups, so the parse that validates
a rule is the parse that builds it. It carries regression tests for
both the panic and the misparse.

Found through AI-assisted code review. The transcripts above are real
output from kubectl v1.36.0 and from a `./cmd/kubectl` build of master
at 400031d6953.

/kind bug
/sig cli

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version --client
Client Version: v1.36.0
Kustomize Version: v5.8.1
```

Also reproduced with a source build of master at 400031d6953:

```console
$ ./kubectl version --client
Client Version: v0.0.0-master+$Format:%H$
Kustomize Version: v5.8.1
```

</details>

### Cloud provider

<details>

N/A - client-side argument parsing, reproduced with `--dry-run=client`.

</details>

<details>

$ uname -a
Darwin 25.5.0 arm64
```

Not OS specific.

{\"status\":\"Degraded\",\"reason\":\"missing_controller\",\"message\":\"missing controller for k8s\"}" pod="default/test-sc-poly-csi-nvme-554fccf545-s5jls"
```

It seems like volume health check started, then volume got deleted, and then health check failed.
Kubelet got `NodeGetVolumeHealthResponse` with 2 messages containing the same `reason`, and then it just got stuck.
I lost the CSI driver logs of this call, but the pod has been stuck for several hours, and for the last few hours CSI driver does not report any NodeGetVolumeHealth calls for this volume, so it seems like kubelet got an invalid value once, and it's indefinitely trying to write it to storage, blocking pod deletion.

The easiest way to resolve this was to restart the kubelet.

### What did you expect to happen?

1. When kubelet gets invalid volume health status, it should repeat NodeGetVolumeHealth before retrying to write it to apiserver.
2. Kubelet should not run NodeGetVolumeHealth and NodeUnstageVolume for the same volume simultaneously. As I see in the CSI spec, concurrent calls for the same volume should only happen if CO loses state ([spec](https://github.com/container-storage-interface/spec/blob/master/spec.md?#concurrency)). I don't have a proof that I got parallel calls for this volume, but I don't know how else I could get error messages like "all connection to storage backend is lost" right at the moment of pod deletion.
3. If kubelet somehow gets volume health status after starting pod shutdown, it should discard it.
4. In general, I don't see why one invalid state update blocks other updates. I would expect that if there are 2 different actions going on (updating `.status` and pod deletion) and one of the actions is failing, then kubelet would add the failed action to backlog and proceed, instead of blocking other actions.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I don't have a ready-to-use reproducer because I got this error seemingly as a consequence of a race condition between NodeGetVolumeHealth and NodeUnstageVolume CSI calls, using an internally developed CSI plugin.
I think it should be reproducible with any volume health report with 2 messages with the same `reason`.
For example:
```json
[{"message":"missing controller for storage","reason":"missing_controller","status":"Degraded"},{"message":"missing controller for k8s","reason":"missing_controller","status":"Degraded"}]
```

title: scheduler: allow a caller-supplied SharedDRAManager
body:
**What would you like to be added?**

A `WithSharedDRAManager` option on `scheduler.New`, so a caller can supply its own `fwk.SharedDRAManager`. With none supplied, nothing changes. Same shape as `WithNodeInfoSnapshot` (#139926).

**Why is this needed?**

`frameworkruntime.WithSharedDRAManager` already accepts a manager, and the interface is documented as the way to simulate DRA state. `scheduler.New` is the only place that hard-codes what gets passed to it.

Kueue admits Workloads before their Pods exist, so it builds ResourceClaims from a PodSet template and needs the DRA plugin to judge those, not the cluster's. It can't today, so it calls `structured.Allocator` directly and the two can drift.

Same gap downstream in kubernetes-sigs/scheduler-library#34, fixed in kubernetes-sigs/scheduler-library#35.

/sig scheduling

title: Kubelet emits spurious Pod status updates due to nondeterministic allocated resource health ordering
body:
### What happened?

With `ResourceHealthStatus` enabled, kubelet can change the order of entries in `status.containerStatuses[*].allocatedResourcesStatus` even when device and claim health have not changed.

There are two nondeterministic paths in kubelet v1.36.3:

1. The device manager constructs each `ResourceStatus.Resources` slice by iterating a map of device IDs. The same resource IDs can therefore be emitted in a different order on later syncs.
2. The DRA manager rebuilds `AllocatedResourcesStatus` by iterating `resourceStatusMap`. This can reorder device-plugin and claim statuses, for example:

```text
[nvidia.com/gpu, claim:channel]
[claim:channel, nvidia.com/gpu]
```

The resulting Pod status is semantically unchanged but serialized differently. Kubelet treats it as a status change and sends a Pod status update. The API server then stores a new resource version and broadcasts a full `MODIFIED` watch event. This can create continuous status and watch churn for otherwise unchanged Pods.

### What did you expect to happen?

Kubelet should produce a stable `AllocatedResourcesStatus` representation when resource health is unchanged. Both the outer `[]ResourceStatus` and each inner `[]ResourceHealth` should have deterministic ordering, so repeated syncs do not cause unnecessary Pod status updates.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Run kubelet v1.36.3 with `ResourceHealthStatus` enabled.
2. Start a Pod whose container has at least two device-plugin devices and a DRA resource claim with health reporting. Generic test device-plugin and DRA drivers are sufficient.
3. Keep all reported health values unchanged.
4. Trigger or wait for repeated Pod status syncs and watch:

```console
kubectl get pod <pod> -w -o json
```

5. Observe that either:
   - entries in a `ResourceStatus.Resources` slice change order, or
   - entries in `AllocatedResourcesStatus` change order.

The Pod `resourceVersion` advances and a `MODIFIED` watch event is emitted despite no health change.

This can also be reproduced in unit tests by calling the two `UpdateAllocatedResourcesStatus` implementations repeatedly with multiple map entries and asserting that their output is canonical.

### Anything else we need to know?

The relevant v1.36.3 code paths are:

- Device ID map iteration while constructing `ResourceStatus.Resources`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/49c14f82ca9748897f0189be31cbf9c2f4085fc1/pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/manager.go#L1162-L1177
- DRA map iteration while rebuilding `AllocatedResourcesStatus`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/49c14f82ca9748897f0189be31cbf9c2f4085fc1/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/manager.go#L936-L943
- The device-manager-then-DRA call order: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/49c14f82ca9748897f0189be31cbf9c2f4085fc1/pkg/kubelet/cm/container_manager_linux.go#L1135-L1145

A minimal fix is to canonicalize the final status by `ResourceStatus.Name` and each resource list by `ResourceHealth.ResourceID`, with regression tests covering stable output across repeated calls.

title: kubectl create quota and set resources accept empty resource names
body:
### What happened?

`kubectl create quota --hard` and `kubectl set resources --limits/--requests` accept resource list entries with an empty resource name. For example:

```console
kubectl create quota demo --hard==1 --dry-run=client -o yaml
```

The command succeeds and produces a ResourceQuota whose `.spec.hard` map contains an empty-string key:

```yaml
spec:
  hard:
    "": "1"
```

The same parser path is used by `kubectl set resources` (`parseResourceList`), so `--limits==1` / `--requests==1` are accepted the same way.

This is inconsistent with nearby validation: `parseScopes` already rejects an empty quota scope (`""`), and `ParseLiteralSource` rejects a leading `=` for configmap/secret literals.

### What did you expect to happen?

The command should reject `<resource>=<value>` entries when the resource name is empty, instead of creating a ResourceList keyed by `""`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run:

```console
kubectl create quota demo --hard==1 --dry-run=client -o yaml
```

The command currently succeeds with an empty hard resource name.

At the unit level, `populateResourceListV1("=1")` in `staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create_quota.go` returns a non-nil ResourceList and no error. The twin helper `parseResourceList` in `staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/set/set_resources.go` has the same gap.

### Anything else we need to know?

`populateResourceListV1` / `parseResourceList` split on `=` and only check that there are exactly two parts. They do not reject `parts[0] == ""`. A client-side fix can reject empty resource names and add regression coverage in the existing quota / set-resources tests.

Originally filed at kubernetes/kubectl#1884; moved here because kubectl code contributions and tracking belong in kubernetes/kubernetes (kubectl is a staged read-only mirror).

title: `GetOldObject` not implemented by `admission.VersionedAttributes`
body:
### What happened?

While implementing and testing https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137633; I realized that `admission.VersionedAttributes` does not override the `GetOldObject` method, which is used for admission webhooks. This means that the embedded `admission.Attributes`' `GetOldObject()` method actually becomes used, and returns the internal object (if core type) or previously stored (if CRD).

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/90b175c8760fcdfea7b9757fb3c366bbe1d4a1fa/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/conversion.go#L55-L60

/sig api-machinery

I expected `GetOldObject` to be implemented for `VersionedAttributed`, so that the versioned old object is returned, not the unversioned one. It should work similarly to `GetObject`

title: kubectl describe pod prints nothing for clusterTrustBundle and podCertificate projected volume sources
body:
### What happened?

`kubectl describe pod` prints nothing for a projected volume source of type `clusterTrustBundle` or `podCertificate`. The volume is listed, but the block ends after the `Type:` line, so there is no indication of what is actually projected into the pod:

```
Volumes:
  creds:
    Type:  Projected (a volume that contains injected data from multiple sources)
```

Projected sources of type `secret`, `configMap`, `downwardAPI` and `serviceAccountToken` are printed as usual.

Both of the affected sources are GA and on by default since v1.37 (`ClusterTrustBundleProjection` and `PodCertificateRequest` in `pkg/features/kube_features.go`, both marked `LockToDefault in 1.38`), so this is not gated-off output.

Cause: `printProjectedVolumeSource` is an `if / else if` chain over the four source kinds it knows about, with no branch for `ClusterTrustBundle` or `PodCertificate` and no fallback, so those entries are silently skipped:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/58cd835870c09a025a9ee4974ec5d8e9e2415e25/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go#L1076-L1097

`describeVolumes` itself already handles every `VolumeSource` kind and has a `default: <unknown>` arm; only the per-projection switch is incomplete.

### What did you expect to happen?

The projected sources to be listed in the same style as the other kinds, for example:

```
Volumes:
  creds:
    Type:                          Projected (a volume that contains injected data from multiple sources)
    ClusterTrustBundleName:        my-bundle
    Path:                          trust-bundle.pem
    Optional:                      false
    PodCertificateSignerName:      example.com/signer
    KeyType:                       ED25519
    CredentialBundlePath:          credentials.pem
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

No cluster feature configuration is needed on v1.37+. Create a pod with a projected volume:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: projected-creds
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - name: creds
      mountPath: /var/run/creds
  volumes:
  - name: creds
    projected:
      sources:
      - clusterTrustBundle:
          name: my-bundle
          path: trust-bundle.pem
      - podCertificate:
          signerName: example.com/signer
          keyType: ED25519
          credentialBundlePath: credentials.pem
```

```console
$ kubectl describe pod projected-creds | grep -A5 Volumes:
```

The `creds:` block stops after the `Type:` line.

At the unit level, describing a pod whose only volume is a projected volume with a `clusterTrustBundle` source produces output containing neither the bundle name nor the path.

### Anything else we need to know?

This is the same class of gap as #142208 (`fileKeyRef` missing from the container env output): a source kind added to the API without a matching arm in the describer.

`podCertificate` is the more user-visible of the two, since a pod does not start until certificates have been issued for every `podCertificate` source in its spec, and `kubectl describe pod` is the first place an operator looks when a pod is stuck.

I have a fix with unit tests and will open a PR shortly.

title: Node Declared Features: allow a feature to opt out of re-admission enforcement after kubelet restart
body:
### What would you like to be added?

An extension to the Node Declared Features (NDF, KEP-5328) framework so that an individual feature can distinguish *first admission* of a pod from *re-admission* of a pod that was already admitted on this node before a kubelet restart, and choose not to require the feature in the latter case.

Today `Feature.InferForScheduling(podInfo *types.PodInfo)` receives only `Spec` and `Status`, and the same call is used in three places:

- scheduler `PreFilter` / `SignPod` (`pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodedeclaredfeatures/nodedeclaredfeatures.go`), with `PodInfo{Spec}` only,
- kubelet first admission (`pkg/kubelet/lifecycle/handlers.go`, `declaredFeaturesAdmitHandler.Admit`),
- kubelet re-admission after restart, which goes through exactly the same `HandlePodAdditions -> allocationManager.AddPod -> canAdmitPod -> Admit` path.

There is no signal available to the feature that would let it tell the last two apart.

Proposed change (prototyped, all additive, no behavior change for existing features):

1. `types.PodInfo` gets a new field `PreviouslyAdmitted bool` ("the kubelet holds a persisted allocation for this pod from an earlier admission; always false during scheduling").
2. `lifecycle.PodAdmitAttributes` gets `PreviouslyAllocated bool`.
3. `allocation.manager.canAdmitPod` populates it from `m.HasPodAllocatedResources(pod.UID)`. The allocation manager restores its `allocated_pods_state` checkpoint synchronously in `NewManager`, before the sync loop starts, and `canAdmitPod` runs before `SetAllocatedResources`, so on first admission the value is `false` and on re-admission after restart it is `true`. Since `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` is GA and locked to `true` in 1.35, this checkpoint is always present; it stores an entry for every admitted pod (including BestEffort), keyed by pod UID.
4. `declaredFeaturesAdmitHandler.Admit` copies the flag into `PodInfo`.

A feature that wants "soft" re-admission then implements:

```go
func (f *myFeature) InferForScheduling(podInfo *types.PodInfo) bool {
    if podInfo.PreviouslyAdmitted {
        return false
    }
    return podUsesFeature(podInfo.Spec)
}
```

### Why is this needed?

KEP-5328 currently documents a single, fail-closed policy for kubelet restarts:

> Node declared features are checked by the scheduler during scheduling and then validated again by the Kubelet's admission handlers before a pod's containers can start. This validation is critical for handling cases where a node's declared features change after a pod has been scheduled.
>
>If a Kubelet restarts with a different configuration (e.g., a feature gate is disabled), its declared features may change. Upon restart, the Kubelet re-evaluates all existing pods for admission and if a running pod requires a declared feature that the node no longer provides, the Kubelet's admission check will fail. Consequently, the pod will not be started and will be transitioned to a `Failed` phase. This ensures that a pod does not run on a node that cannot support its feature requirements. This behavior is consistent with the best practice of draining a node before making significant configuration changes, such as toggling feature gates.
>
> — keps/sig-node/5328-node-declared-features/README.md:440-442

This is the correct default for most NDF features: if the node can no longer provide something the pod fundamentally depends on, the pod should be evicted.

However, there is a class of features where this is unnecessarily disruptive:

- the feature only affects pod setup and is irrelevant once the pod is running, or
- the feature provides optional, additive functionality that a running pod can simply lose without breaking.

An example is KEP-6122 (Configurable Scaling Delay, targeting Alpha in v1.38). It uses NDF in its intended role: a kubelet with `InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUsScaleDownDelay` enabled declares the feature in `node.status.declaredFeatures`, and the scheduler only places pods that set `scaleDownGracePeriodSeconds` on nodes that declare it, so a pod never lands on a node that would silently ignore its grace period. The same KEP explicitly departs from the KEP-5328 default for one case ("Grace Period Not Honored" section): when the gate is turned off on a node that already runs such a pod and the kubelet restarts, the pod is not rejected, because killing a running latency-sensitive workload is worse than resizing it without the preparation window. The kubelet is instead expected to apply the next scale-down without the delay and report it via the `PodResizeInProgress` condition message and a `ScaleDownGracePeriodNotHonored` event. Its PRR rollback answer is built on this: existing pods keep running, only the delay is lost.

With today's NDF framework that behaviour cannot be implemented. The scheduler's node filter and the kubelet's admission check are driven by the same `Feature.InferForScheduling` method, so a feature that returns `true` to obtain scheduler filtering also gets fatal kubelet re-admission after a restart with the gate disabled: the pod fails with `PodFeatureUnsupported` and is killed.

title: Client-go: Add support for Connection Pool
body:
### What would you like to be added?

I would like to propose adding a support to client-go library for creating multiple connections **to the same endpoint** and using some naive load balancing (such as round robin or power of 2) to send traffic.

The option cloud be set using one of the following mechanisms:
* In kubeconfig, via option similar to 'disableCompression' we have today
* In golang, by setting respective value, e.g. via rest.Config flag

Goal:
* In many environments, the endpoint specified in kubeconfig is an L4 load balancer that picks backend randomly. By opening multiple connections we can split the traffic from a single client / controller to multiple kube-apiserver replicas and avoid single kube-apiserver instance becoming overloaded while the other replicas are idle.
* Avoid single-replica pinning issue -- improve client experience in case of single kube-apiserver replica slowdown / unhealthiness. E.g. today kubelet sends traffic only to a single kcp replica. if the replica is slow or unhealthy (e.g. not able to process requests but alive), all connections are persistent and all kubelet's retries are still going to that replica, leading to marking the replica as unhealthy. By sending traffic to multiple replicas, we increase chances (both must be unhealthy).

Out of scope:
* Multiple endpoint support (we still want client-go to open connections to single endpoint -- we rely on L4 load balancer to assign connections to multiple backends)
* Endpoint discovery: Client-go somehow finds out what are the IPs for kube-apiserver instances.

### Why is this needed?

This is important use case for performance-heavy controllers / schedulers and similar technique is widely used by the components (see e.g. [transportHack](https://github.com/kubernetes/perf-tests/blob/1317eb81116835070beecdb2f6cb4eda3fd27b1c/clusterloader2/pkg/framework/config/client_config.go#L86) in clusterloader).

By moving this concept to core client-go library we can help the controllers to avoid this "transportHack" or similar technique. By standardising this pattern, we can make this opinionated and ensure that controllers are behaving in expected way and automatically benefit from potential improvements in this area.

body:
### Which jobs are flaking?

pull-kubernetes-kind-dra-all, an optional presubmit. The periodic ci-kind-dra-all has not shown this in two weeks.

Triage: https://storage.googleapis.com/k8s-triage/index.html?pr=1&job=pull-kubernetes-kind-dra-all%24&text=TLS%20handshake%20timeout%7Chttp2%3A%20client%20connection%20lost

### Which tests are flaking?

In [run 2103785290568044544](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/pr-logs/pull/142411/pull-kubernetes-kind-dra-all/2103785290568044544) 149 specs passed, 2 specs failed, and the ReportAfterSuite Log Check also failed. They were `verifies cgroup inflation and container OOM adjustment with overhead mappings` and `does not delete generated claims when pod is restarting`. Both failed in `DeferCleanup` steps that could not reach the apiserver, one deleting a ServiceAccount and one in the driver builder:

```
[FAILED] deleting ServiceAccount.v1 dra-node-allocatable-resources-6568/dra-kubelet-plugin-dra-9dee3718f9e05859-service-account: Delete "https://127.0.0.1:40963/api/v1/namespaces/dra-node-allocatable-resources-6568/serviceaccounts/dra-kubelet-plugin-dra-9dee3718f9e05859-service-account": http2: client connection lost
In [DeferCleanup (Each)] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/dra/utils/deploy.go:933 @ 09/26/26 10:24:54.647
```

Expected: the cleanup deletes its objects and the suite ends green. Actual: the client gets `http2: client connection lost` or `TLS handshake timeout`. The Log Check fails too, because its pod listing timed out twice and because the kubelet on kind-worker2 reported a data race, filed as [#142439](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142439).

In the two weeks to 2026-09-26, 19 of 143 completed runs hit one of those errors, 15 after [#142127](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142127) merged.

### Since when has it been flaking?

At least since 2026-09-14 in the triage data.

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-presubmits#pull-kubernetes-kind-dra-all

### Reason for failure (if possible)

The whole job stalls for up to a minute, and the API errors are what the test client sees during the stall. My best guess for the stall itself is CPU starvation under the pod's 2 CPU quota, and the evidence for that guess follows.

From 10:24:13Z to 10:25:12Z, kubelet log lines on all four kind nodes reach the journal up to 42 seconds late. containerd on kind-worker2 fails a task delete with `context deadline exceeded`, etcd logs a read-only apply that took 16.9 s, and kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler both lose their lease and restart. Apiserver and etcd did not restart, nothing was OOM killed, and etcd logs no slow disk sync.

Runs [2102022370477740032](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/pr-logs/pull/142277/pull-kubernetes-kind-dra-all/2102022370477740032) and [2101978783241211904](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/pr-logs/pull/141917/pull-kubernetes-kind-dra-all/2101978783241211904) from 2026-09-21 look the same, only worse: etcd applies of 45 to 52 s and repeated controller-manager restarts. A green run of the same PR shows none of this.

The podlogs fixes from [#141962](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141962) and [#142127](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142127) are in the base of that run, and [#142026](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142026) was closed as not needed yet.

The pod runs four race-enabled kind nodes and eight race-enabled ginkgo workers under a 2 CPU / 12Gi limit, and the kind node processes still size themselves to the node's CPU count ([kubernetes/test-infra#37733](https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/37733) fixed the runner leaf only).

A local replay with the same image, script and limits had 93% of its CFS periods throttled during the test phase and used 1.93 of its 2 cores. Control-plane log lines fell up to 18.7 s behind, the apiserver logged handler timeouts, and the run also ended with two failed specs plus a Log Check race, though the two failures were timeouts, not transport errors. It did not reproduce the lease losses, the transport errors or the cAdvisor race.

A control run with the quota raised to 8 CPUs had no throttled periods, used 2.75 cores and passed all 151 specs with a clean Log Check.

CI ran its specs in 1018 s under the same quota while the local replay needed 2349 s, so the workstation is slower than the Prow node for this job and the local percentages do not transfer one to one.

### Anything else we need to know?

As far as I can tell the same stalls take cAdvisor's `statfs` wrapper into its timeout path, which exposes the kubelet race in [#142439](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142439).

This issue was written in part with the assistance of generative AI. The analysis and the local replay ran on my workstation and I reviewed the results.

title: cloud-controller-manager accepts the NativeHistograms feature gate but never applies it
body:
### What happened?

`NativeHistograms` (KEP-5808) is Beta and enabled by default since v1.37. Each component must call
`metricsfeatures.ApplyFeatureGates()` for histograms to pick up the gate state:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6c1c7702cf2052245ef10e699d45f071af306f59/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/features/kube_features.go#L51-L56

This is done in kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kube-proxy and kubelet,
the five components listed in KEP-5808.

However, `k8s.io/cloud-provider/app` also registers the metrics feature gates, so
cloud-controller-manager accepts `--feature-gates=NativeHistograms=true` and
`DefaultFeatureGate.Enabled(NativeHistograms)` returns true, but nothing calls
`ApplyFeatureGates`:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6c1c7702cf2052245ef10e699d45f071af306f59/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/app/controllermanager.go#L68-L71

So on every cloud-controller-manager built on `k8s.io/cloud-provider/app`, the gate reports as
enabled (by default since v1.37) but has no effect, and histograms stay classic-only.
The same is true in v1.37.0.

### What did you expect to happen?

Either cloud-controller-manager histograms are exposed in both classic and native formats when
`NativeHistograms` is enabled, like the other control-plane components, or, if
cloud-controller-manager is intentionally out of scope, the gate should not silently appear
enabled there with no effect.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

No cluster is needed. This test drives the real `NewCloudControllerManagerCommand` and checks,
from the `cloudInitializer` hook (which runs after `Config()`), whether a newly created
histogram is native:

<details>
<summary>Test snippet</summary>

```go
cloudInitializer := func(*config.CompletedConfig) cloudprovider.Interface {
	gateEnabled := utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate.Enabled(metricsfeatures.NativeHistograms)
	nativeBefore := histogramIsNative(t, "repro_before_seconds") // NewHistogram + Gather, checks Schema != nil
	metricsfeatures.ApplyFeatureGates(utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate)
	nativeAfter := histogramIsNative(t, "repro_after_seconds")
	// ...
}
cmd := app.NewCloudControllerManagerCommand(s, cloudInitializer, app.DefaultInitFuncConstructors,
	names.CCMControllerAliases(), cliflag.NamedFlagSets{}, stopCh)
cmd.SetArgs([]string{"--kubeconfig=<dummy>", "--cloud-provider=fake",
	"--feature-gates=NativeHistograms=true", "--secure-port=0", "--webhook-secure-port=0"})
```

</details>

Output at master (6c1c7702cf2):

```
NativeHistograms gate enabled in CCM:                true
histogram native after CCM startup (Config done):   false
histogram native after calling ApplyFeatureGates:    true
```

I'm happy to share the full test.

### Anything else we need to know?

I noticed that KEP-5808 lists only five components, so I'm not sure whether leaving out
cloud-controller-manager was a deliberate scoping decision. Either way, the gate currently
looks enabled but silently does nothing there, which seems worth resolving in one of two ways:

1. Wire it up: call `features.ApplyFeatureGates(utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate)` in the
   cloud-controller-manager `RunE`, right after `logsapi.ValidateAndApply`. That is before
   `s.Config()` builds REST clients and informers, so it also avoids the ordering problem
   described in #142379. A cloud-controller-manager case could be added to
   `test/integration/metrics/nativehistograms/metrics_test.go`.
2. If cloud-controller-manager is intentionally out of scope, make that explicit, for example
   in the KEP or the feature-gate docs, so cloud-provider maintainers aren't surprised.

Happy to send a PR for option 1 if that's the preferred direction.

Related: #128842, #142379, #142377.

AI tools assisted with the investigation; I reviewed the code and ran the reproduction myself.

/sig cloud-provider
/sig instrumentation

### Kubernetes version

<details>

Reproduced from source at master 6c1c7702cf2052245ef10e699d45f071af306f59 (v1.38 development).
Confirmed the same code is in v1.37.0 (`ApplyFeatureGates` is not called in `k8s.io/cloud-provider/app`).

</details>

### Cloud provider

<details>
Any cloud-controller-manager built on `k8s.io/cloud-provider/app`. Reproduced with a unit test, so no cloud is involved.
</details>

### OS version

Windows 11 (build 26200), go1.27.1. Not OS-specific.

title: apimachinery yaml: last line silently dropped when its length is a multiple of the buffer size
body:
### What happened?

`k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/yaml` silently drops the last line of a stream when that line has no trailing newline and its length is an exact multiple of the reader's buffer size (4096 in `NewYAMLOrJSONDecoder(r, 4096)`). No error is returned, the last document is just truncated.

Cause: `bufio.Reader.ReadLine` never returns data and an error together, so for such a line `LineReader.Read` reads it as full-buffer prefix chunks, then gets `io.EOF` on one extra call and returns the accumulated bytes *with* `io.EOF`. `YAMLReader.Read` treats `io.EOF` as end of data and discards `line`.

### What did you expect to happen?

The final line is returned, whatever its length.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```go
for _, n := range []int{4095, 4096, 4097} {
	last := "b: " + strings.Repeat("x", n-3)
	r := yaml.NewYAMLReader(bufio.NewReaderSize(strings.NewReader("a: 1\n---\n"+last), 4096))
	r.Read()
	doc, err := r.Read()
	fmt.Println(n, len(doc), err)
}
// 4095 4096 <nil>
// 4096 0 EOF     <- document lost
// 4097 4098 <nil>
```

### Anything else we need to know?

Hit in production through Argo CD: its config-management-plugin server `TrimSuffix`es the plugin output's trailing newline before splitting it with `NewYAMLOrJSONDecoder(..., 4096)`. A Helm chart whose last rendered line was a 16384-byte JSON `spec:` (victoria-metrics-operator-crds 0.15.0) was applied without its `spec`, and the API server rejected the object.

Present on master and in every release I tested (v0.34.1 to v0.36.1). Fix with a regression test to follow.

### Kubernetes version

Library bug, reproduced with `k8s.io/apimachinery` v0.34.1, v0.35.3, v0.36.0, v0.36.1 and master.

### Cloud provider

N/A (library).

/sig api-machinery

title: kube-proxy config validation reports internal field paths
body:
### What happened?

kube-proxy configuration validation reports error field paths using internal Go type and field names instead of the public `kubeproxy.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1` JSON/YAML field names.

For example, a config with invalid values for:

```yaml
apiVersion: kubeproxy.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: KubeProxyConfiguration
bindAddress: "10.10.12.11:2000"
healthzBindAddress: "0.0.0.0"
metricsBindAddress: "127.0.0.1"
iptables:
  masqueradeBit: 32
```

is reported by the validator as:

```text
KubeProxyConfiguration.KubeProxyIPTablesConfiguration.MasqueradeBit: Invalid value: 32: must be within the range [0, 31]
KubeProxyConfiguration.BindAddress: Invalid value: "10.10.12.11:2000": not a valid textual representation of an IP address
KubeProxyConfiguration.HealthzBindAddress: Invalid value: "0.0.0.0": must be IP:port
KubeProxyConfiguration.MetricsBindAddress: Invalid value: "127.0.0.1": must be IP:port
```

Those paths do not match the fields users put in kube-proxy config files:

```text
iptables.masqueradeBit
bindAddress
healthzBindAddress
metricsBindAddress
```

The same pattern appears in other kube-proxy validation paths, for example:

- `KubeProxyConfiguration.KubeProxyLinuxConfiguration.KubeProxyConntrackConfiguration.TCPEstablishedTimeout` instead of `conntrack.tcpEstablishedTimeout`
- `KubeProxyConfiguration.KubeProxyLinuxConfiguration.OOMScoreAdj` instead of `oomScoreAdj`
- `KubeProxyConfiguration.KubeProxyIPVSConfiguration.ExcludeCidrs` instead of `ipvs.excludeCIDRs`

The external field names are defined in `staging/src/k8s.io/kube-proxy/config/v1alpha1/types.go`, but `pkg/proxy/apis/config/validation/validation.go` constructs paths with internal names like:

```go
field.NewPath("KubeProxyConfiguration")
newPath.Child("BindAddress")
newPath.Child("KubeProxyIPTablesConfiguration")
fldPath.Child("MasqueradeBit")
```

The current unit tests also assert these internal paths, for example `pkg/proxy/apis/config/validation/validation_test.go` expects `BindAddress`, `KubeIPTablesConfiguration.MasqueradeBit`, and `KubeProxyLinuxConfiguration.KubeProxyConntrackConfiguration.*`.

### What did you expect to happen?

Validation errors for kube-proxy config should identify the public config file field paths, so users can copy the path back into their YAML/JSON and find the bad field directly.

Examples:

```text
iptables.masqueradeBit: Invalid value: 32: must be within the range [0, 31]
bindAddress: Invalid value: "10.10.12.11:2000": not a valid textual representation of an IP address
healthzBindAddress: Invalid value: "0.0.0.0": must be IP:port
metricsBindAddress: Invalid value: "127.0.0.1": must be IP:port
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

No cluster is required; this is pure kube-proxy config validation.

I reproduced on current master (`feb5375e`) by adding a temporary test under `pkg/proxy/apis/config/validation` that builds an otherwise valid `KubeProxyConfiguration`, sets invalid values for `BindAddress`, `HealthzBindAddress`, `MetricsBindAddress`, and `IPTables.MasqueradeBit`, then logs `Validate(config).ToAggregate()`.

The focused command:

```bash
mise exec go@1.27.0 -- go test ./pkg/proxy/apis/config/validation -run '^TestIssueReproKubeProxyConfigErrorPaths$' -count=1 -v
```

printed:

```text
[KubeProxyConfiguration.KubeProxyIPTablesConfiguration.MasqueradeBit: Invalid value: 32: must be within the range [0, 31], KubeProxyConfiguration.BindAddress: Invalid value: "10.10.12.11:2000": not a valid textual representation of an IP address, KubeProxyConfiguration.HealthzBindAddress: Invalid value: "0.0.0.0": must be IP:port, KubeProxyConfiguration.MetricsBindAddress: Invalid value: "127.0.0.1": must be IP:port]
```

The existing validation tests show the same paths without adding a repro test; for example:

```bash
mise exec go@1.27.0 -- go test ./pkg/proxy/apis/config/validation -run 'TestValidateKubeProxyConfiguration/invalid BindAddress|TestValidateKubeProxyIPTablesConfiguration|TestValidateKubeProxyIPVSConfiguration|TestValidateKubeProxyLinuxConfiguration' -count=1
```

passes today because the expected errors use the internal paths.

### Anything else we need to know?

This looks similar in shape to incorrect validation field path issues elsewhere: clients and users consume these paths as references to configuration fields, so they should match the external API surface rather than internal Go names.

Possible fix direction: make kube-proxy validation construct paths from the public v1alpha1 config layout (`bindAddress`, `iptables.masqueradeBit`, `ipvs.excludeCIDRs`, `conntrack.tcpEstablishedTimeout`, etc.) and update the validation tests accordingly.

Analysis prepared with AI assistance and verified with local code inspection plus the focused Go test above.
