title: Scheduling queue: gated pod group is requeued on events its gating plugin's QueueingHint skips
body:
### What happened?

A pod group gated by a PreEnqueue plugin is taken out of `unschedulableEntities`, run through PreEnqueue again and put back on events for which the gating plugin's QueueingHint returns `QueueSkip`. PreEnqueue gates the group again, so no wrong scheduling decision is made, but the work is wasted and `scheduler_queue_incoming_pods_total{queue="unschedulable"}` grows by the size of the group on every such event.

**Cause.** [`isPodWorthRequeuing`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/625d634722837a25981f28888bfc7245932c817c/pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L584-L588) returns `queueAfterBackoff` for a pod whose `UnschedulablePlugins` and `PendingPlugins` are both empty, without consulting any QueueingHint, and [`isEntityWorthRequeuing`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/625d634722837a25981f28888bfc7245932c817c/pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L556-L575) returns the strongest result across the pods of the group. A gated pod has its gating plugin in `UnschedulablePlugins` ([`runPreEnqueuePlugin`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/625d634722837a25981f28888bfc7245932c817c/pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L783-L788)), so the gating plugin's hint decides for that pod. But a gated group can also contain pods with no rejector plugins at all, and a single such pod makes the whole group return `queueAfterBackoff`, overriding the gating plugin's `QueueSkip`. There are two kinds of such pods:

1. **Pods added while the group is gated.** A gated group stays in `unschedulableEntities`. For a group found there, [`addToPodGroupIfExists`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/625d634722837a25981f28888bfc7245932c817c/pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L956-L973) adds the pod and keeps the group in place (strategy `queueSkip` from [`deleteFromAnyQueue`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/625d634722837a25981f28888bfc7245932c817c/pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L940-L952)) without running PreEnqueue; only a group found in activeQ or backoffQ goes through `moveToActiveQ`/`moveToBackoffQ`, which run it. Since #141577, [`runPreEnqueuePlugins`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/625d634722837a25981f28888bfc7245932c817c/pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L703-L731) stops at the first gated pod, so later requeue attempts don't evaluate these pods either while that pod stays gated. Before #141577, the next requeue attempt recorded the gating plugin for them, which limited this to one extra requeue per joining pod.

   Example: a gang with `minCount: 4` whose pods are created one by one. GangScheduling's PreEnqueue gates every pod of the gang until quorum is met.

   1. p1 is created. PreEnqueue gates the group, which goes to `unschedulableEntities`; p1's `UnschedulablePlugins` is `{GangScheduling}`.
   2. p2 and p3 are created and join the group in `unschedulableEntities` without running PreEnqueue, so their `UnschedulablePlugins` stay empty.
   3. A pod outside the gang is created or bound anywhere in the cluster. GangScheduling registers `UnscheduledPod/Add` and `AssignedPod/Add` ([EventsToRegister](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/625d634722837a25981f28888bfc7245932c817c/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/gangscheduling/gangscheduling.go#L65-L85), [eventhandlers.go#L244](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/625d634722837a25981f28888bfc7245932c817c/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L244), [eventhandlers.go#L422](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/625d634722837a25981f28888bfc7245932c817c/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L422)), so the group is evaluated. GangScheduling's hint returns `QueueSkip` for p1, but p2's empty set returns `queueAfterBackoff`, so the group is requeued, and PreEnqueue gates it again at p1. Since #141577 it stops there, so p2 and p3 stay empty.
   4. Step 3 repeats on every pod creation and binding in the cluster until the gang reaches quorum. The same happens to every other waiting gang that already has more than one pod.

2. **Pods that pass PreEnqueue and haven't been attempted yet.** PreEnqueue records a plugin only when it rejects the pod, and apart from that the sets are filled only by a failed scheduling attempt, which a gated group doesn't get. So a pod that passes PreEnqueue has empty sets for as long as its group stays gated, and running PreEnqueue on it again doesn't change that: this cause doesn't depend on #141577. It needs a gating plugin that decides per pod, such as DynamicResources or SchedulingGates; GangScheduling decides for the whole group at once.

   Example: p1 and p2 are in one pod group. p1 uses no ResourceClaims; p2 uses a ResourceClaimTemplate, and its ResourceClaim hasn't been created yet.

   1. DynamicResources' [PreEnqueue](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/625d634722837a25981f28888bfc7245932c817c/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/dynamicresources/dynamicresources.go#L292-L297) rejects p2 because its claim doesn't exist, and accepts p1. The group is gated; p2's `UnschedulablePlugins` is `{DynamicResources}`, p1's is empty.
   2. A ResourceClaim of an unrelated pod is created or updated. DynamicResources registers ResourceClaim events, so the group is evaluated. DynamicResources' [hint](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/625d634722837a25981f28888bfc7245932c817c/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/dynamicresources/dynamicresources.go#L408-L437) returns `QueueSkip` for p2, but p1's empty set returns `queueAfterBackoff`, so the group is requeued, and PreEnqueue gates it again because of p2. p1's set stays empty, since p1 passes PreEnqueue.
   3. Step 2 repeats on every ResourceClaim change in the cluster until p2's claim is created.

### What did you expect to happen?

A gated pod group is requeued only by an event that can ungate it: when the QueueingHint of a gated pod's gating plugin returns `Queue`, or on a wildcard event.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Unit test on top of master: `TestMoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueueGatedGang` in `pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/scheduling_queue_test.go` on https://github.com/Argh4k/kubernetes/tree/gated-pg-repro. It reproduces the cause 1 example with the GangScheduling plugin and its QueueingHints:

1. It creates a PodGroup with `minCount: 4` and adds p1, p2 and p3 the way the scheduler's event handler does (`Add`, then `MoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue` with `UnscheduledPod/Add`). The gang is gated, and only p1 has `GangScheduling` in `UnschedulablePlugins`.
2. It calls `MoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue` with `UnscheduledPod/Add` for three pods outside the gang and checks that PreEnqueue isn't called again.

```console
$ go test ./pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/ -run TestMoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueueGatedGang -v
=== RUN   TestMoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueueGatedGang
    scheduling_queue_test.go:8445: Expected 3 pods added outside the gang not to requeue the gated gang, but PreEnqueue ran 3 more times; UnschedulablePlugins per pod: map[p1:[GangScheduling] p2:[] p3:[]]
--- FAIL: TestMoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueueGatedGang (0.11s)
FAIL
```

### Anything else we need to know?

- The unschedulable branch of [`PriorityQueue.Update`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/625d634722837a25981f28888bfc7245932c817c/pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L1449-L1463) calls `isEntityWorthRequeuing` for gated entities without the gating-events filter that [`moveEntitiesToActiveOrBackoffQueue`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/625d634722837a25981f28888bfc7245932c817c/pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L1820-L1827) applies, so any update of a member pod has the same effect.
- Running PreEnqueue on every pod again (reverting #141577) would limit cause 1 to one extra requeue per joining pod and would not fix cause 2. Letting only the gated pods' hints decide for a gated entity would cover both.

title: kube-proxy can lose the initial node topology event and ignore zone hints until restart
body:
/sig network
/kind bug

### What happened?

On AKS and EKS, kube-proxy repeatedly logged this warning:

```text
"Ignoring same-zone topology hints for service since node is missing label" label="topology.kubernetes.io/zone"
```

On the affected nodes, the Node API object had the correct zone label. The services used `spec.trafficDistribution: PreferSameZone`. Their EndpointSlices had ready endpoints with valid hints for both zones.

The installed iptables ClusterIP chains selected endpoints from both zones. A restart of only the affected kube-proxy pod restored zone-local selection:

| Environment | Service | Before proxy restart | After proxy restart |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AKS | Service A | 1 local + 1 remote | 1 local |
| AKS | Service B | 2 local + 2 remote | 2 local |
| EKS | Service A | 2 local + 2 remote | 2 local |
| EKS | Service C | 4 local + 4 remote | 4 local |
| EKS | Service D | 3 local + 3 remote | 3 local |

The counts describe installed rules (`KUBE-SVC` → `KUBE-SEP` → DNAT), not measured traffic.

On AKS, repeated rule syncs did not restore locality before the restart. Node labels and the relevant EndpointSlices did not change. Later syncs kept the correct selection.

On EKS Datadog recorded 11,100 matching warnings in 24 hours.
A same-zone control proxy with the same image and node pool selected only local endpoints.
Both proxies processed an endpoint update, but the affected proxy continued to ignore zone hints.

Restarting only kube-proxy on EKS restored same-zone routing for all seven service ports. The node, proxy image, service configuration, and endpoints stayed unchanged.
Routing remained correct nearly three minutes later, after eight rule syncs, with no missing-label warnings.

### What did you expect to happen?

A valid Node zone label must reach the proxier, including its initial state. Endpoint selection must honor same-zone hints for ready endpoints.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Using unchanged Kubernetes v1.35.5 topology-config code and a real client-go informer with a fake client, we forced initial Node replay before consumer registration. Across 20 runs, the consumer received no zone after an unchanged-zone update, while registration before replay delivered the zone in all control runs.

### Anything else we need to know?

#### Suspected startup ordering problem

In v1.35.5, [`NewNodeManager` starts and syncs the Node informer](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6636cbce3bbef91ff61d36658757179426f9e1b2/pkg/proxy/node.go#L69-L86). Then [server startup creates `NodeTopologyConfig` and registers the proxier](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6636cbce3bbef91ff61d36658757179426f9e1b2/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go#L611-L617). The [constructor attaches its callback to the running informer](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6636cbce3bbef91ff61d36658757179426f9e1b2/pkg/proxy/config/config.go#L473-L499), so the cached Node can arrive before registration. [`handleNodeEvent` stores the zone even with no consumers](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6636cbce3bbef91ff61d36658757179426f9e1b2/pkg/proxy/config/config.go#L516-L530). If replay arrives first, later same-zone events return at `reflect.DeepEqual`, and the proxier never gets the zone.

This order matches the warning and the restart recovery. We did not capture the event order in an affected process, so the link to the incident is a hypothesis.

The order comes from [PR #133059](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133059), included since v1.34.0 GA. We did not test v1.34. The relevant topology-config code is identical in v1.35.3 and v1.35.5. The order remains at master [`def85dfe8aabea42fa1569ad5c4f60de5b976fdd`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/def85dfe8aabea42fa1569ad5c4f60de5b976fdd/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go#L634-L639).

A possible fix: register the topology consumer before the callback can receive informer events.

### Kubernetes version

| Environment | kube-proxy image | kubelet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AKS | `v1.35.5-16` | `v1.35.5` |
| EKS | `v1.35.3-eksbuild.2` | `v1.35.6-eks-bca9cf6` |

The EKS control plane reported `1.35`, with no patch version. The reproducer uses upstream v1.35.5 and client-go v0.35.5.

title: kubectl: OpenAPI v3 query param verifier fails on typed List resources (e.g. ReplicationControllerList, ServiceList) and falls back to OpenAPI v2
body:
### What happened?

When validating a typed `*List` resource (such as `v1.ReplicationControllerList` or `v1.ServiceList`), `queryParamVerifierV3.HasSupport` looks up `/openapi/v3/api/v1` and searches `supportsQueryParamV3` for a `PATCH` endpoint matching the GVK. Because list kinds do not have a `PATCH` endpoint, `supportsQueryParamV3` returns a generic error (`Path not found for GVK (/v1, Kind=ReplicationControllerList) in OpenAPI V3 doc`) instead of `ParamUnsupportedError`.

As a result:
1. With `FallbackQueryParamVerifier`, `kubectl` treats this as an OpenAPI v3 failure and erroneously falls back to downloading the entire deprecated `/openapi/v2` schema (`GET /openapi/v2`).
2. Without the OpenAPI v2 fallback, `kubectl create` / `kubectl apply` fails validation on typed `*List` manifests with `error validating data: Path not found for GVK (/v1, Kind=ReplicationControllerList) in OpenAPI V3 doc`.

### What did you expect to happen?

`supportsQueryParamV3` should return `ParamUnsupportedError` when a GVK has no `PATCH` endpoint in its `GroupVersion`'s OpenAPI v3 spec, without failing validation or falling back to `/openapi/v2`.

### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run `kubectl create` with `--validate=warn` and `-v=6` on a `ReplicationControllerList` or `ServiceList` manifest:

```bash
kubectl create --validate=warn --dry-run=client -v=6 -f hack/testdata/multi-resource-rclist.json
```

Observe in the `-v=6` logs that after fetching `/openapi/v3/api/v1`, `kubectl` falls back to `GET https://<server>/openapi/v2` because `queryParamVerifierV3` failed with `Path not found for GVK (/v1, Kind=ReplicationControllerList) in OpenAPI V3 doc`.

/kind bug
/sig cli

title: pkg/controller: reduce allocations in FilterPodsByOwner
body:
### What would you like to be added?

`controller.FilterPodsByOwner` collects the Pods returned by the owned and orphaned indexer lookups into a result slice that starts empty and is grown by repeated appends. For an owner with thousands of Pods, most of the allocated bytes in the call are growth copies rather than the Pods themselves.

The size of both index lookups is known before any Pod is copied. The result can be allocated once with capacity `len(owned) + len(orphaned)` and filled from the two lookup results, keeping the current order (owned Pods first, orphaned Pods after) and error handling.

### Why is this needed?

`FilterPodsByOwner` is called by the Deployment, ReplicaSet, StatefulSet, DaemonSet and Job controllers on every sync, and by the Deployment controller once per ReplicaSet. With large workloads this is a steady source of short-lived allocations in the controller loops.

I added `BenchmarkFilterPodsByOwner` to `pkg/controller` and compared the current implementation with a version that preallocates the result (windows/amd64, AMD Ryzen 5 6600H, `-benchmem -count=8`):

| benchmark | time (before to after) | B/op (before to after) | allocs/op (before to after) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10 owned | 1086 ns to 936 ns (-13.8%) | 384 to 272 (-29.2%) | 4 to 3 (-25.0%) |
| 10000 owned | 767 us to 704 us (-8.2%) | 463 KiB to 240 KiB (-48.2%) | 17 to 3 (-82.4%) |
| 10000 owned + 10000 orphaned | 1.79 ms to 1.45 ms (-18.6%) | 1063 KiB to 480 KiB (-54.9%) | 22 to 4 (-81.8%) |

Geomean across the three cases: time -13.7%, B/op -45.1%, allocs/op -71.1%.

The change is a refactor of the helper with no behavior change, and the benchmark is included so the numbers can be reproduced with `go test ./pkg/controller/ -run NONE -bench BenchmarkFilterPodsByOwner -benchmem`.

title: Kubelet fails to start when an unrelated mountinfo entry has an empty mount source
body:
### What happened?


Kubelet can fail during startup when `/proc/self/mountinfo` contains an entry
whose mount source is empty, even when that entry is unrelated to the kubelet
root directory.

Linux accepts an empty source for pseudo filesystems. For example, a caller can
create a sysfs mount with:

```go
syscall.Mount("", target, "sysfs", 0, "")
```

The corresponding mountinfo tail contains an empty field:

```text
- sysfs  rw
```

`mount.ParseMountInfo` currently tokenizes the complete line with
`strings.Fields`. That collapses the empty source, leaving only two fields
after the `-` separator. Parsing then fails with an error similar to:

```text
expect 3 fields in ... - sysfs  rw, got 2
```

During startup, kubelet calls:

```text
setupDataDirs
  -> MakeRShared
  -> findMountInfo
  -> ParseMountInfo
```

`findMountInfo` parses every mountinfo entry before selecting the mount that
contains the kubelet root directory. As a result, an unrelated temporary mount
under `/tmp` can prevent kubelet from checking the propagation of
`/var/lib/kubelet` and cause kubelet to exit.


### What did you expect to happen?


Kubelet should determine the mount containing its root directory without
requiring filesystem-specific fields from unrelated mountinfo entries.

An explicitly empty mount source should be preserved as an empty field rather
than removed during tokenization.

If the selected mount entry is incomplete or cannot be parsed safely, kubelet
should still return an error.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?


On the current Kubernetes source tree, add this regression test to
`pkg/volume/util/hostutil/hostutil_linux_test.go`:

```go
func TestIsSharedWithEmptySourceOnUnrelatedMount(t *testing.T) {
	mountInfo := `62 0 253:0 / / rw,relatime shared:1 - ext4 /dev/root rw
7334 62 0:5118 / /tmp/empty-source-sysfs rw,relatime shared:30 - sysfs  rw
`
	tempDir, filename, err := writeFile(mountInfo)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer os.RemoveAll(tempDir)

	if _, err := isShared("/var/lib/kubelet", filename); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

Run:

```console
$ go test ./pkg/volume/util/hostutil -run TestIsSharedWithEmptySourceOnUnrelatedMount -count=1
--- FAIL: TestIsSharedWithEmptySourceOnUnrelatedMount
    hostutil_linux_test.go:...: expect 3 fields in ... - sysfs  rw, got 2
FAIL
```

The failing entry is unrelated to `/var/lib/kubelet`; the root mount already
contains the requested path and has valid `shared:` metadata.

### Anything else we need to know?


The kubelet propagation check only needs the mount point and optional
propagation fields for the mount containing the requested path. It does not
need the source, filesystem type, or superblock options from every unrelated
entry.

A safe lookup can:

1. Validate the six mandatory mountinfo prefix fields for every entry.
2. Select the last mount point that is an ancestor of the requested path.
3. Parse the optional fields and filesystem-specific tail only for the selected
   entry.
4. Continue to fail closed if the selected entry is incomplete.

The generic full-file parser should preserve an explicitly empty source by
splitting the raw line around the ` - ` separator before tokenizing the tail.

Mountinfo escapes spaces and backslashes in path fields. A path-specific lookup
also needs to account for escapes such as `\040` when matching a requested
path.

This is similar in impact to
[kubernetes/kubernetes#135554](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/135554),
but that issue concerns unescaped spaces in `/proc/mounts`. This report concerns
an empty source in `/proc/self/mountinfo` and kubelet's root mount propagation
lookup.

### Kubernetes version


<details>

```console
$ git rev-parse HEAD
b3c29caa02988dc0e560428c016b7e5d30f702a5
```

The behavior is also present in Kubernetes v1.35-derived kubelet code.



### Cloud provider


<details>

Not provider-specific.

</details>


### OS version


<details>

Linux. The deterministic reproducer above uses a mountinfo fixture and does not
depend on a specific distribution.

</details>

### Install tools


<details>

Not applicable.

</details>

### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)


<details>

Not runtime-specific. The failure occurs while kubelet initializes its root
directory.

</details>

### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)


<details>

The condition can be triggered by any privileged component that creates a
pseudo-filesystem mount with an empty source. The parser behavior is not
specific to a particular plugin.

</details>


/sig node
/sig storage

title: HPA selector overlap check repeatedly serializes identical pod labels
body:
### What happened?

`HPAsMatchingPods` calls `labels.Set.String()` for every pod before deduplicating label sets. Pods from the same ReplicaSet commonly have identical labels, so this repeatedly allocates and sorts the same data during HPA reconciliation.

This remains in [current master](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8f5bbad3e20a347aaae13afd78cc955e642c68e4/pkg/controller/podautoscaler/hpa_selector_store.go#L114-L122), after the selector-store change in #139142.

### What did you expect to happen?

Avoid repeated serialization when all pods have the same labels, while preserving matching for mixed label sets.

### How can we reproduce it?

Run the existing benchmark:

```sh
GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./pkg/controller/podautoscaler -run '^$' \
  -bench '^BenchmarkHPAsMatchingPodsParallel$/1000hpas_' -benchmem
```

With 1,000 HPA selectors, increasing identically labeled pods from 10 to 100 increases allocations from 31 to 301 per operation. The proposed fast path reduces both to 4.

### Environment

Local package benchmarks on Linux/amd64, Go 1.27.3. No cluster-level performance claim. Timings were collected at cb9115192fc; the affected code is unchanged at 8f5bbad3e20.

/sig autoscaling
/kind cleanup

title: NodeResourcesFit scorer ignores PodLevelResources and in-place resize feature gates
body:
### What happened?

The `NodeResourcesFit` plugin builds its `resourceAllocationScorer` (used for the `LeastAllocated`, `MostAllocated` and `RequestedToCapacityRatio` strategies) in `NewFit`. It only propagates `EnableDRAExtendedResource` to the scorer. `enablePodLevelResources`, `enableInPlacePodVerticalScaling` and `enableInPlacePodLevelResourcesVerticalScaling` are never set, so they are always `false` when the scorer computes pod requests.

As a result, even when the corresponding feature gates are enabled, Fit scoring:
- ignores pod-level resources (`spec.resources`) and scores on aggregated container requests only;
- ignores in-progress and pending resizes (status/allocated resources) when computing pod requests.

`NodeResourcesBalancedAllocation` constructs its scorer directly and propagates these features correctly, so the two scoring plugins can disagree for the same pod.

### What did you expect to happen?

The Fit scorer should honor the `PodLevelResources`, `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` and `InPlacePodLevelResourcesVerticalScaling` feature gates, the same way the Fit filter and `BalancedAllocation` do.

### Anything else we need to know?

See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142959#discussion_r4279630125.

/sig scheduling node
/kind bug
/cc @pravk03 @dom4ha
/assign @ndixita

title: DRA device taint eviction ignores DeviceToleration with empty effect, although the API says empty matches all effects
body:
### What happened?


A claim request with a `DeviceToleration` that has no `effect` does not protect the pod from a `NoExecute` device taint. 
The device taint eviction controller evicts the pod as if there were no toleration.


Observed on a v1.37.1 cluster with the example driver, same key/value taint, one claim+pod per row:

| Rule (toleration with empty effect, `operator: Exists`) | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| vs `NoSchedule` taint, at allocation | tolerated, claim allocates | tolerated, claim allocates |
| vs `NoExecute` taint, at eviction | tolerated, pod stays | **pod evicted** |

`kubectl explain resourceclaim.spec.devices.requests.exactly.tolerations.effect` on the cluster says: 
"Effect indicates the taint effect to match. Empty means match all taint effects." 
The tolerations field text adds that "should any of the allocated devices get tainted with NoExecute after allocation and that effect is not tolerated, then all pods consuming the ResourceClaim get deleted", which an empty-effect toleration should satisfy.


The KEP-5055 API definition has the same text ("Effect indicates the taint effect to match. Empty means match all taint effects."), and I couldn't find anything in the KEP or the release notes that says empty should behave differently for eviction.

So the empty effect is honored at allocation and only the eviction controller disagrees.



### What did you expect to happen?

A toleration with empty effect that matches the taint key/value tolerates the NoExecute taint, same as one with `effect: NoExecute`.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Cluster with DRA and the example driver (4 devices). Four claims, each used by one running pod, tolerations on the request:

```yaml
tolerations:
- {key: example.com/incident-response, operator: Exists}                       # a: empty effect
- {key: example.com/incident-response, operator: Exists, effect: NoExecute}    # b: control
```

Then:

```yaml
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: DeviceTaintRule
metadata: {name: repro}
spec:
  deviceSelector: {driver: gpu.example.com}
  taint: {key: example.com/incident-response, value: "true", effect: NoExecute}
```

Pod `a` gets `DeviceTaintManagerEviction ... Marking for deletion` within seconds; pod `b` keeps running.

Unit test: adding a case to `TestController` with a toleration `{Operator: Exists}` and no effect (sibling "no-evict-pod-toleration-forever" case, but without `Effect`) fails with an eviction scheduled; the same case with `Effect: NoExecute` passes.

### Which jobs are failing?

- https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-containerd#cos-containerd-main-node-features

```
failed to create shim task: OCI runtime create failed: unable to retrieve OCI runtime error (open /run/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/k8s.io/<id>/log.json: no such file or directory): /home/containerd/usr/local/sbin/runc did not terminate successfully: exit status 1
```

and on the ci-containerd-e2e-ubuntu-gce master, `kube-master-installation` fails at the `runc --version` check.

The tarball `gs://k8s-staging-cri-tools/containerd/main/containerd-cni-2.4.0-154-g57d315c6e.linux-amd64.tar.gz` was overwritten in place at 2026-10-24T06:02:57Z (same version string, same containerd commit) by `ci-containerd-build`. That run (2113873277536440320) used `kubekins-e2e:v20261019-e80425793a-master`, which is based on Debian 13 trixie (glibc 2.41). The previous run (2113692002745847808) used `kubekins-e2e:v20261012-c0cc6281b1-master` on Debian 12 bookworm (glibc 2.36). runc is dynamically linked, so it now requires glibc >= 2.38, which COS 121/129 do not ship.

Same failure class as #142987 (arm64 AL2023), now hitting amd64 via the kubekins base image bump. Possible fixes: build runc statically in the containerd build job, or pin `ci-containerd-build` / `post-containerd-build` to a bookworm-based image.

title: Request to backport PR #143253 to v1.37
body:
Can we backport PR #143253, which fixes #143252, to v1.37 once it merges?

With `PodGroupPreemptionPolicy` enabled, creating a PodGroup or CompositePodGroup that references a PriorityClass with `preemptionPolicy: Never` is rejected when the group omits its own policy. title: CertificateSigningRequest spec updates report success but are silently discarded; the immutability check from #142354 cannot fire
body:
### What happened?

The spec of a CertificateSigningRequest (CSR) is immutable after creation. But instead of rejecting a change to it — as the [API conventions](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#considerations-for-put-operations) require ("Be careful to detect and report legitimate errors where the 'new' value is specified but is different from the 'old' value") and as other kinds with immutable fields do — kube-apiserver discards the change silently and reports success:

- `kubectl patch` says `patched (no change)`
- `kubectl apply` says `configured`
- `kubectl replace` says `replaced`

and the stored value never changes. The client gets no error and no warning, so it has no way to learn that its change was discarded. For contrast, changing the immutable `spec.controller` of an IngressClass is rejected with `field is immutable` (shown below).

Where: `csrStrategy.PrepareForUpdate` (`pkg/registry/certificates/certificates/strategy.go`) does `newCSR.Spec = oldCSR.Spec`.

A fix was merged for 1.38 (#142354: an immutability check on `spec`; CSR is also listed in the KEP-5073 immutable-fields migration, #136785), but it cannot fire: kube-apiserver runs `PrepareForUpdate` BEFORE validation (`staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/registry/rest/update.go`, `BeforeUpdate`), so the check compares the already-reset spec with itself. The PR's tests never go through `PrepareForUpdate`: the unit test calls `ValidateCertificateSigningRequestUpdate` directly, and the declarative-validation test calls `rest.ValidateUpdate` rather than `rest.BeforeUpdate`, which is why they pass. The 1.38 pre-releases (verified on v1.38.0-alpha.3) behave exactly like 1.37.

### What did you expect to happen?

An update that changes an immutable CSR `spec` field should be rejected with an error (as `IngressClass`, `PersistentVolume` and others do), not reported as a success.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Two containers, no cluster needed: etcd + kube-apiserver at the version under test. Setting them up — step 1 (key material and kubeconfig) and step 2 (starting etcd and kube-apiserver) — is in [REPRO.txt](https://github.com/munachimso-victor/UrsaPublic/blob/main/manual_tests/csr_silent_drop_repro/REPRO.txt). Then create a CSR with `spec.expirationSeconds: 86400` and try to change it to 3600 three ways:

```sh
openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout req.key -subj "/CN=csr-drop-test" -out req.csr
cat > csr.yaml <<EOF
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: csr-silent-drop-test
spec:
  request: $(base64 -w0 req.csr)
  signerName: kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client
  expirationSeconds: 86400
  usages:
  - client auth
EOF
kubectl apply -f csr.yaml
# certificatesigningrequest.certificates.k8s.io/csr-silent-drop-test created
kubectl patch csr csr-silent-drop-test --type json \
  -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/expirationSeconds","value":3600}]'
# certificatesigningrequest.certificates.k8s.io/csr-silent-drop-test patched (no change)
sed 's/expirationSeconds: 86400/expirationSeconds: 3600/' csr.yaml | kubectl apply -f -
# certificatesigningrequest.certificates.k8s.io/csr-silent-drop-test configured
kubectl get csr csr-silent-drop-test -o yaml | sed 's/expirationSeconds: 86400/expirationSeconds: 3600/' | kubectl replace -f -
# certificatesigningrequest.certificates.k8s.io/csr-silent-drop-test replaced
kubectl get csr csr-silent-drop-test -o jsonpath='{.spec.expirationSeconds}{"\n"}'
# 86400   <- after every one of the three
```

Contrast, the same kind of change on an IngressClass is rejected:

```sh
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: IngressClass
metadata:
  name: contrast
spec:
  controller: example.com/a
EOF
# ingressclass.networking.k8s.io/contrast created
kubectl patch ingressclass contrast --type merge -p '{"spec":{"controller":"example.com/b"}}'
# The IngressClass "contrast" is invalid: spec.controller: Invalid value: "example.com/b": field is immutable
```

Terminal logs of the full step-by-step run: [v1.37.2](https://github.com/munachimso-victor/UrsaPublic/blob/main/manual_tests/csr_silent_drop_repro/sample_log_v1.37.2.txt) and [v1.38.0-alpha.3](https://github.com/munachimso-victor/UrsaPublic/blob/main/manual_tests/csr_silent_drop_repro/sample_log_v1.38.0-alpha.3.txt).

### Anything else we need to know?

We found this while researching a testing tool for multi-cluster orchestrators (systems that manage many Kubernetes clusters). The tool makes the same change directly on a plain single cluster and uses that cluster as the reference for what the multi-cluster system should end up with. Because the tool trusts the single cluster to be accurate, this went unnoticed until we manually checked whether the updates had actually taken place.

We first saw it in our test fleet (v1.29.8) and in a manual reproduction on v1.37.2. While investigating, we found the fix merged in #142354, but v1.38.0-alpha.3, which includes it, still discards the change. Our tests run on kind, which does not publish node images for Kubernetes pre-releases, so we tested v1.38.0-alpha.3 against the upstream kube-apiserver image directly.

Because our testing tool runs on kind, which publishes node images only for stable releases (no alphas or betas), we can only use a fix once it ships in a release. Could the real fix be backported to 1.37 (for example 1.37.3), or land before the 1.38 code freeze (16 November) so that it is in 1.38.0 (due 16 December)? Otherwise 1.38 would ship with the current check, which cannot fire.

### Reason for failure (if possible)

Pods never start; the container is stuck in `CreateContainerError`:

```
Failed: Error: grpc: error unmarshalling request: string field contains invalid UTF-8
```

#139172 extended these tests so the Secret contains a non-UTF-8 value (`0x80`) that is injected via `env.valueFrom` and `envFrom`.

The kubelet side is fine: #139168 changed CRI `KeyValue.value` from `string` to `bytes` (in master and `k8s.io/cri-api` v0.36.2). The job, however, runs `cri-o://1.36.0` (commit `d1e7bdc8`), which vendors `k8s.io/cri-api v0.36.0-rc.0`. There the field is still `string`, so CRI-O's gRPC server rejects the request during unmarshal.

The commit range `aabdf5a22..1356a818e` contains #143354, #142093, #141771 and #139172. Only #139172 touches this code path.

### Anything else we need to know?

#139172 noted that kind needed containerd v2.3.4+ for the same reason. CRI-O wasn't mentioned.

Possible fixes:
1. Bump the CRI-O used by this job to a build vendoring `k8s.io/cri-api` >= v0.36.2.
2. Revert #139172, or gate the binary-value assertions, until the CRI-O image is updated.

These are `[Conformance]` tests, so the new assertions imply a minimum runtime version. That may need sig-node/sig-architecture input.

Related: #139132, #139168, #139172

title: Consider deprecating or changing the default of --service-account-extend-token-expiration
body:
### What would you like to be added?
Consider changing the default of `--service-account-extend-token-expiration` to `false` in a future release, or deprecating the flag, now that the migration it was added for is long over. If sig-auth agrees on a direction, I'm happy to pick this up, including writing a KEP or the implementation PR.

### Why is this needed?
The flag's help text says it "helps safe transition from legacy token to bound service account token feature" and that "admission injected tokens would be extended up to 1 year to prevent unexpected failure during transition" ([source](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f3a4bbacc08a3c89673419b8d3db272540160ed1/pkg/kubeapiserver/options/authentication.go#L459-L463)). Bound service account tokens went beta in 1.21, about 5 years ago. It defaults to `true`, so injected tokens are accepted for far longer than the 1 hour the pod spec implies.

Consequences of the default:
- Clients that read the token once and cache it keep working silently for the extended window and then fail all at once. With the extension off, they would fail within about an hour, where they are easy to find.
- A token that has been rotated away but leaked stays usable until the pod is deleted or the extended window ends.
- CIS Kubernetes Benchmark control 1.2.30 recommends setting it to `false`, so many distributions have to override the default to pass audits.

Managed services (EKS, GKE) run with the default and do not expose the flag. We see the extension active on both (non-zero `serviceaccount_stale_tokens_total`), so users of managed clusters cannot opt out of what upstream treats as a temporary measure. Related: aws/containers-roadmap#2899. AWS actually sets to 90d instead of 1y default


Presumably this could be a breaking change for those who do not upgrade their package versions and EKS, GKE, AKS and any other provider that does not allow this value to configure would need to add support for any such use cases where it is desired to be keep as true 


/kind feature
/sig auth

title: NNN is not cleared in some Workload Aware Preemption scenarios
body:
### What happened?

/sig scheduling
/assign @ania-borowiec

Bug in [submitPodGroupResult](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e3e26fc7ab75352979c1498f1dca7ee7eaf41c23/pkg/scheduler/schedule_one_podgroup.go#L886):
When a pod in a PodGroup fails `SchedulePod` with `*framework.FitError`, `schedulingAlgorithm()` returns `ScheduleResult{nominatingInfo: nil}` and defers clearing NNN to `submitPodGroupAlgorithmResult`. Skipped pods in `completePodGroupAlgorithmResult` also get `nominatingInfo: nil`. However, `submitPodGroupResult` only passes `clearNominatedNode` when `podResult.status.IsSuccess() `is `true` and the group failed; for pods where `!podResult.status.IsSuccess()`, line 936 passes `podResult.scheduleResult.nominatingInfo` (nil, i.e., fwk.ModeNoop) to `FailureHandler`. Consequently, stale NNN is never cleared on pods that fail Filter when preemption does not nominate a node for them.

This was discovered when writing new integration tests for NNN with podgroup preemption, see exact scenarios in the section below.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected NNN to be cleared in the scenarios described below.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This was discovered when working on additional integration tests. I want to extend [TestPodGroupPreemptionAndNominatedNodeNameScenarios](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2505ca4641e78ca94df6b4451029a7e03a258b5f/test/integration/scheduler/nominated_node_name/nominated_node_name_test.go#L622) with scenarios similar to the ones in [TestPreemptionAndNominatedNodeNameScenarios](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2505ca4641e78ca94df6b4451029a7e03a258b5f/test/integration/scheduler/nominated_node_name/nominated_node_name_test.go#L316C6-L316C49):

Scenario 1: Clearing stale NNN when scheduling fails (similar to  "NNN is ignored on pod that cannot fit on the node")

createNode: node1 with capacity 4 CPU.
createPodGroup: gang pg-exceeds (lowPriority, minCount: 2)
Create pg-exceeds pods with NNN: createPods: exceeds-1 (lowPriority, 3 CPU) and exceeds-2 (lowPriority, 3 CPU) in pg-exceeds, with nominatedNodeName: "node1".
createPodGroup: gang pg-fits (lowPriority, minCount: 2).
Create pg-fits pods without NNN: createPods: fits-1 (lowPriority, 2 CPU) and fits-2 (lowPriority, 2 CPU) in pg-fits, no NNN.
schedulePodGroup for pg-exceeds (exceeds-1, exceeds-2).
pg-exceeds is at the head of activeQ because it was created before pg-fits.
pg-exceeds fails scheduling (total 6 CPU > 4 CPU) and fails PodGroupPostFilter (no victims).
When AddAttemptedPodGroupIfNeeded requeues pg-exceeds, its timestamp is updated to clock.Now(), placing it behind pg-fits in activeQ.
checkNNN on pg-exceeds pods: exceeds-1, exceeds-2 with expectedNNN: "".
Schedule pg-fits: schedulePodGroup for pg-fits (fits-1, fits-2).
Verify pg-fits scheduled: verifyPodsScheduled for fits-1, fits-2 on node1.


Scenario 2: Clearing NNN on lower-priority nominated pods (similar to "NNN is ignored on lower priority pod when higher priority pod without NNN is being scheduled")

createNode: node1 with capacity 3 CPU.
createPodGroup: gang pg-low (lowPriority, minCount: 3).
createPodGroup: gang pg-high (highPriority, minCount: 3).
createPods: low-1, low-2, low-3 in pg-low (lowPriority, 1 CPU each), with nominatedNodeName: "node1".
createPods: high-1, high-2, high-3 in pg-high (highPriority, 1 CPU each), no NNN.
schedulePodGroup for pg-high (high-1, high-2, high-3).
RunFilterPluginsWithNominatedPods ignores pg-low's nominations on node1 because lowPriority < highPriority.
verifyPodsScheduled for high-1, high-2, high-3 on node1.
schedulePodGroup for pg-low (low-1, low-2, low-3).
pg-low fails Filter (node occupied by pg-high) and fails PodGroupPostFilter (cannot preempt higher-priority pg-high).
Check NNN cleared on pg-low: checkNNN for low-1, low-2, low-3 with expectedNNN: ""

title: DeviceTaintEvictionController counts a pod that is already terminating as evicted
body:
### What happened?

When a pod is scheduled for eviction because of a `NoExecute` device taint, and someone else starts deleting it before the eviction fires, `DeviceTaintEvictionController` still counts it as evicted.

`addConditionAndDeletePod` in `pkg/controller/devicetainteviction/device_taint_eviction.go` gets the pod, sees `DeletionTimestamp` set, and returns nil without adding the condition, emitting the event or deleting the pod. `maybeDeletePod` cannot tell that apart from a successful delete, so it increments `device_taint_eviction_controller_pod_deletions_total`, observes `device_taint_eviction_controller_pod_deletion_duration_seconds`, and increments `numEvictedPods` for each `DeviceTaintRule` involved, which ends up in the rule status as "N pods evicted since starting the controller."

The `NotFound` branch right above already skips these updates, with the comment "we didn't do it, so don't bump the metric". The terminating case needs the same.

This is reachable without any race, for any pod that stays terminating for a while because of its grace period or a finalizer. `podEvictionTime` does not check `DeletionTimestamp`, so a pod that is already terminating when the taint arrives still gets queued. And `handlePodChange` ignores updates that only set `DeletionTimestamp`, so a pod whose deletion starts during its toleration period stays queued too.

### What did you expect to happen?

A pod that is already terminating is not counted in the deletion metrics or in the `DeviceTaintRule` evicted pod count, the same as a pod that is already gone.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Start the controller with a pod that uses a device with a `NoExecute` taint and is already terminating, held by a finalizer. The controller queues the eviction, makes no delete call and emits no event, but `device_taint_eviction_controller_pod_deletions_total` is 1 and the latency histogram has one sample. I checked this with the fake clientset in a unit test on master.

### Anything else we need to know?

The `DeletionTimestamp` check was added in c69259cb713 ("DRA device taints: switch to workqueue in controller"), first released in v1.35.0.

I have a fix with a regression test and will open a PR shortly.

title: CVE-2026-116472: ingress-nginx mirror-target self-DOS
body:
CVSS Rating: **2.7** (LOW) [CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L)

A security issue was discovered in ingress-nginx where a user with permission to create an Ingress may be able to cause denial of service of the ingress-nginx data plane, or possibly redirect traffic from other Ingresses. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they are using ingress-nginx.

Due to a missing check, the mirror-target Ingress annotation can be used to target an unauthenticated configuration API within the ingress-nginx controller, allowing write commands to be submitted. Corrupting the data within that configuration API results in all traffic through ingress-nginx being dropped until an Ingress configuration change or a controller restart causes the data to be recreated correctly.

In principle, this write access could also be used to redirect traffic from other Ingresses controlled by the same ingress-nginx instance. In practice, there is negligible additional risk: such redirection would require privileged information about internal ingress-nginx state, and users can already redirect traffic from other Ingresses controlled by the same ingress-nginx anyway.

Kubernetes will not be issuing a fix for this CVE, because ingress-nginx maintenance ended in March 2026.

SUSE has issued a fix for this CVE in version 1.15.2-prime1 of their fork of ingress-nginx.

### Am I vulnerable?

This issue affects ingress-nginx. If you do not have ingress-nginx installed on your cluster, you are not affected. You can check this by running `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --selector app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx`.

### How do I mitigate this vulnerability?

Prior to upgrading, this vulnerability can be mitigated by using an admission controller to reject Ingresses that specify the mirror-target annotation, or by setting the annotations-risk-level configMap parameter to "Medium" or "Low".

#### How to upgrade?

To upgrade, consult the documentation provided by your vendor.

Note that the Kubernetes project will not be issuing a fix for this CVE.

### Detection

Localhost addresses in the mirror-target annotation of an Ingress resource may indicate an attempt to exploit this vulnerability.

If you find evidence that this vulnerability has been exploited, please contact **security@kubernetes.io**

#### Acknowledgements

This vulnerability was reported by Victor Pereira.

title: Uncached OpenAPI v3 schemas cause 41+ unmarshals on a 20-resource apply
body:
### What happened?

Applying updates to an existing 20-resource `core/v1` manifest (`kubectl apply -f`) unmarshals the `1.53 MB` `api/v1` OpenAPI v3 JSON **41 to 47 times**, causing **351–406 MB of cumulative heap allocations (`~8.5 MB` per unmarshal, `~800–900 ms` CPU)**:
- **20 `ConfigMap`s (1 `Kind`):** **41 unmarshals** (`1` in `queryParamVerifierV3` + `40` in `Patcher`) = **`351.6 MB` `TotalAlloc` (`785 ms`)**.
- **20 `core/v1` resources across 7 `Kind`s:** **47 unmarshals** (`7` in `queryParamVerifierV3` + `40` in `Patcher`) = **`406.2 MB` `TotalAlloc` (`905 ms`)**.
- **20 Custom Resources of a CRD:** **21 full CRD schema unmarshals** just to check `paths` and learn Strategic Merge Patch is unsupported.

Root cause: `k8s.io/client-go/openapi/cached` only caches raw JSON `[]byte`, `openapi3.Root.GVSpec(gv)` (`client-go/openapi3/root.go:95-104`) runs `json.Unmarshal` on every call, and `kubectl`'s `factoryImpl` constructs a new `openapi3` client per caller instead of sharing a cached GVK-indexed resource map like OpenAPI v2 (`factory_client_access.go:182-217`).

Because `client-go/openapi3` lacks a shared `?hash=` (`ServerRelativeURL()`)-keyed, GVK-indexed cache, other `k8s.io` packages have already had to hand-roll private caches (`client-go/applyconfigurations/meta/v1/unstructured.go`, `apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/policy/mutating/patch/typeconverter.go`), and downstream controllers hit the same repeated unmarshaling (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubectl/issues/1894).

### What did you expect to happen?

`k8s.io/client-go/openapi3` should provide a shared, `?hash=`-keyed (`ServerRelativeURL()`), GVK-indexed resource cache so repeated lookups in a `GroupVersion` do not re-unmarshal the entire `GroupVersion` JSON on every call.

/kind bug
/sig cli
/sig api-machinery
/cc @liggitt @Jefftree @soltysh

title: ResourceClaim updates fail with "spec: field is immutable" when opaque parameters are not canonical JSON
body:
### What happened?

A ResourceClaim created with the Python client (kubernetes 37.0.2) cannot be labeled afterwards:

```
$ kubectl label resourceclaim claim-py x=y
The ResourceClaim "claim-py" is invalid: spec: Invalid value: null: field is immutable
```

The client sends `"parameters": {"a": "b", "z": 1}`, and etcd stores those bytes. When the apiserver returns JSON or applies a patch, it re-encodes them as `{"a":"b","z":1}`. The immutable check on `spec` compares bytes, so the update is rejected.

`kubectl annotate`, `kubectl patch --type=merge` and `kubectl replace` fail the same way. After `kubectl delete`, a custom finalizer cannot be removed with kubectl, and the claim stays in deletion. Server-side apply fails even without whitespace if the keys are not sorted. ResourceClaimTemplate has the same problem.

On 1.37.2 the garbage collector cannot orphan such a claim either. After `kubectl delete pod --cascade=orphan` on the owning Pod, the Pod keeps the `orphan` finalizer and kube-controller-manager logs the same error.

### What did you expect to happen?

Metadata changes succeed when the spec is unchanged.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

`claim.json`:

```json
{
  "apiVersion": "resource.k8s.io/v1",
  "kind": "ResourceClaim",
  "metadata": {"name": "claim-raw"},
  "spec": {"devices": {
    "requests": [{"name": "r", "exactly": {"deviceClassName": "cls"}}],
    "config": [{"requests": ["r"], "opaque": {"driver": "driver.example.com", "parameters": {"a": "b", "z": 1}}}]
  }}
}
```

```
kubectl create --raw /apis/resource.k8s.io/v1/namespaces/default/resourceclaims -f claim.json
kubectl label resourceclaim claim-raw x=y
```

The label fails. With `kubectl create -f claim.json` the parameters are stored compact, and the label succeeds.

Results by request type, v1.38.0-beta.0 / v1.37.2, request bodies sent as is:

| `parameters` | merge patch | strategic merge patch | JSON patch | apply | PUT of the GET result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `{"z": 1, "a": "b"}` | 422 / 422 | 200 / 422 | 422 / 422 | 422 / 422 | 422 / 422 |
| `{"z":1,"a":"b"}` | 200 / 200 | 200 / 422 | 200 / 200 | 422 / 422 | 200 / 200 |
| `{"a":"b","z":1}` | 200 / 200 | 200 / 200 | 200 / 200 | 200 / 200 | 200 / 200 |

### Anything else we need to know?

- #73655 is the same problem for ControllerRevision. #142996 tried to fix it there by comparing decoded JSON and was closed by its author before review.
- Strategic merge patch, which the garbage collector uses, stopped failing in 1.38 because #142394 converts only the top-level fields a patch touches.
- PrepareForUpdate could keep the old bytes when the new parameters decode to the same JSON. Claims that are already stored would then work too.

### Kubernetes version

v1.38.0-beta.0 and v1.37.2 (official kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager binaries), etcd v3.7.3, kubectl v1.37.0.

/kind bug
/sig api-machinery
/sig node
/wg device-management

body:
### Which jobs are failing?

[ci-kubernetes-e2e-capz-master-windows](https://prow.k8s.io/job-history/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-capz-master-windows)

### Which tests are failing?

[Kubernetes e2e suite [It] [sig-api-machinery] WebSocket streaming port forwarding over the WebSocket tunnel should forward to a server listening on localhost [Conformance]](https://storage.googleapis.com/k8s-triage/index.html?job=%5Eci-kubernetes-e2e-capz-master-windows%24&test=WebSocket%20streaming%20port%20forwarding%20over%20the%20WebSocket%20tunnel%20should%20forward%20to%20a%20server%20listening%20on%20localhost)

### Since when has it been failing?

2026-11-10 19:00 UTC

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-release-master-informing#capz-windows-master&exclude-non-failed-tests=

### Reason for failure (if possible)

```
[FAILED] data forwarded from the pod
Expected
    <[]uint8 | len:0, cap:512>: ""
to equal
    <[]uint8 | len:100, cap:100>: "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
In [It] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/apimachinery/websocket_streaming.go:285 @ 11/11/26 01:04:34.656

There were additional failures detected after the initial failure. These are visible in the timeline
```

PR [#143780](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143780) promoted these tests to `[Conformance]`, causing them to run on `capz-master-windows` for the first time. The localhost variant was probably never tested on Windows before.

As per https://blog.sixeyed.com/published-ports-on-windows-containers-dont-do-loopback, On Linux, the kernel can forward external requests to a container's loopback address (`127.0.0.1`). On Windows with the NAT network stack, it can't — only `0.0.0.0` works. That's probably why the `0.0.0.0` variant of the test passes and the localhost variant returns empty data

The test assumes Linux networking behavior. On Windows, port-forwarding to a container process bound to `127.0.0.1` silently returns nothing. The fix is probably either skip the localhost test variant on Windows, or change the test's bind address to `0.0.0.0` when running on Windows nodes.

title: Reserve assigns allocation results to the wrong ResourceClaims when a pod mixes a pending shared allocation with a new claim
body:
/kind bug
/sig scheduling
/sig node
/wg device-management

**What happened:**

While studying how the scheduler handles a ResourceClaim shared by two pods in a PodGroup, I hit what looks like a data-correctness bug in the DynamicResources plugin (feature gates `DRAWorkloadResourceClaims=true` + `GenericWorkload=true`, `scheduling.k8s.io/v1alpha2` served).

My test cluster runs two simulated GPUs (`gpu-0`, `gpu-1`) published by the NVIDIA DRA driver on top of nvml-mock (mokka). Two claims, each pinned to exactly one GPU via a CEL selector on the device uuid:

- **shared claim** (generated for the PodGroup from a template): selector pins uuid `GPU-…0000` → only `gpu-0` can ever match
- **`c-own`** (standalone, used only by the second pod): selector pins uuid `GPU-…0001` → only `gpu-1` can ever match

Pods: `p1` uses the shared claim only; `p2` uses `[shared, c-own]` in that order. Both are in the same PodGroup (`schedulingPolicy: basic: {}`) and get scheduled in one cycle, so when `p2` runs Filter/Reserve, the shared claim still carries the *pending* allocation that `p1`'s Reserve produced and PreBind has not published yet.

All evidence below is from a stock kube-scheduler at `-v=5`, no patches. What actually happens:

1. `p1` Reserve: shared ← `gpu-0` (correct)
2. `p2` PreFilter: `reusing pending allocation` for shared, content is `gpu-0` — still correct at this point
3. `p2` Reserve: **shared ← `gpu-1`** and **c-own ← `gpu-0`** — the two results are cross-wired
4. Then one of two outcomes, depending on which pod's binding goroutine runs PreBind first:
   - **p1 wins** (4 of 5 runs): shared gets published with the correct `gpu-0`; `p2`'s PreBind fails with `claim … got allocated elsewhere in the meantime`; `p2` goes to backoff and retries. On retry the shared claim is a plain "already allocated" claim (no pending-allocation path), so everything heals and the final state looks fine — apart from the spurious failure event.
   - **p2 wins** (1 of 5 runs): **the swapped allocations are persisted.** shared is published with `gpu-1`, c-own with `gpu-0`. Now it is `p1`'s PreBind that fails with "allocated elsewhere"; on retry `p1` reuses the already-allocated (wrong) device without validating it against the claim's selectors. Both pods bind and the cluster reports no error anywhere.

Final API state from the run where `p2` won:

```
$ kubectl get resourceclaims -n dra-crosswire-mokka \
    -o custom-columns='CLAIM:.metadata.name,DEVICES:.status.allocation.devices.results[*].device'
CLAIM                   DEVICES
c-own                   gpu-0     # its selector pins uuid …0001 == gpu-1
repro-pg-shared-bgldq   gpu-1     # its selector pins uuid …0000 == gpu-0
```

Both claims now permanently hold a device that their own CEL selector can never select, and both pods are bound on it.

**What did you expect to happen:**

The pending allocation for the shared claim is reused as-is (`gpu-0`), and the fresh allocation is computed for `c-own` (`gpu-1`). Internally reordering results is fine as long as Reserve maps them back to the right claim; the published `status.allocation` of a claim should never violate the claim's own selectors, and PreBind should not fail spuriously.

**How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):**

Single-node Kubernetes v1.36.5 (rke2). Alpha features enabled on apiserver, controller-manager and scheduler, plus runtime config:

```yaml
kube-apiserver-arg:
  - "feature-gates=GenericWorkload=true,DRAWorkloadResourceClaims=true"
  - "runtime-config=scheduling.k8s.io/v1alpha2=true"
kube-controller-manager-arg:
  - "feature-gates=GenericWorkload=true,DRAWorkloadResourceClaims=true"
kube-scheduler-arg:
  - "feature-gates=GenericWorkload=true,DRAWorkloadResourceClaims=true"
```

GPU simulation is not essential to the bug — any DRA driver exposing two distinguishable devices works, allocation itself is driver-agnostic. I used mokka + the NVIDIA GPU DRA driver:

```bash
helm install nvml-mock oci://ghcr.io/nvidia/k8s-test-infra/chart/nvml-mock -n mokka --set gpu.count=2
helm install dra-driver-nvidia-gpu oci://registry.k8s.io/dra-driver-nvidia/charts/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu \
  --version 0.5.1 -n dra-driver-nvidia-gpu --create-namespace \
  --set gpuResourcesEnabledOverride=true \
  --set nvidiaDriverRoot=/var/lib/nvml-mock/driver \
  --set resources.computeDomains.enabled=false
# driver DaemonSet needs an NFD-style label to schedule on the fake-GPU node:
kubectl label node <node> feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-10de.present=true
```

This publishes one ResourceSlice with devices `gpu-0` (uuid `GPU-12345678-…-0000`) and `gpu-1` (uuid `…0001`), and DeviceClass `gpu.nvidia.com`.

Manifests:

```yaml
# shared claim template: pinned to GPU-0
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceClaimTemplate
metadata:
  name: tmpl-shared
  namespace: dra-crosswire-mokka
spec:
  spec:
    devices:
      requests:
        - name: gpu
          exactly:
            deviceClassName: gpu.nvidia.com
            count: 1
            selectors:
              - cel:
                  expression: "device.attributes['gpu.nvidia.com'].uuid == 'GPU-12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456780000'"
---
# own claim for p2 only: pinned to GPU-1
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceClaim
metadata:
  name: c-own
  namespace: dra-crosswire-mokka
spec:
  devices:
    requests:
      - name: gpu
        exactly:
          deviceClassName: gpu.nvidia.com
          count: 1
          selectors:
            - cel:
                expression: "device.attributes['gpu.nvidia.com'].uuid == 'GPU-12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456780001'"
---
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1alpha2
kind: Workload
metadata:
  name: repro-workload
  namespace: dra-crosswire-mokka
spec:
  podGroupTemplates:
    - name: group
      schedulingPolicy:
        basic: {}
      resourceClaims:
        - name: shared
          resourceClaimTemplateName: tmpl-shared
---
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1alpha2
kind: PodGroup
metadata:
  name: repro-pg
  namespace: dra-crosswire-mokka
spec:
  podGroupTemplateRef:
    workload:
      workloadName: repro-workload
      podGroupTemplateName: group
  schedulingPolicy:
    basic: {}
  resourceClaims:
    - name: shared
      resourceClaimTemplateName: tmpl-shared
---
# p1: only the shared claim
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: p1
  namespace: dra-crosswire-mokka
spec:
  schedulingGroup:
    podGroupName: repro-pg
  containers:
    - name: c
      image: nginx:stable
      command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
      resources:
        claims: [{name: shared}]
  resourceClaims:
    - name: shared
      resourceClaimTemplateName: tmpl-shared
---
# p2: shared claim FIRST (pending), own claim SECOND (fresh) — this order is what triggers it
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: p2
  namespace: dra-crosswire-mokka
spec:
  schedulingGroup:
    podGroupName: repro-pg
  containers:
    - name: c
      image: nginx:stable
      command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
      resources:
        claims: [{name: shared}, {name: own}]
  resourceClaims:
    - name: shared
      resourceClaimTemplateName: tmpl-shared
    - name: own
      resourceClaimName: c-own
```

Trigger — make both pods enter scheduling in the *same* cycle, so the shared claim is still pending when `p2` filters:

```bash
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl apply -f pods.yaml        # both pods Pending, PodGroup Unschedulable
kubectl uncordon <node>           # whole group schedules in one cycle
```

Repeat the whole thing a handful of times (delete pods + group claims + PodGroup/Workload in between). The spurious-PreBind-failure variant showed up in almost every run; the persisted-wrong-device variant in about 1 of 5 runs. Run the scheduler with `-v=5` to get the per-claim allocation logs below.

Evidence (kube-scheduler `-v=5`, timestamps trimmed, multi-line allocation JSON inlined):

Run where `p1`'s PreBind won — cross-wiring happens in Reserve, then p2 fails PreBind and heals on retry:

```
06:42:54.217  Reserve.DynamicResources   pod=p1 claim=repro-pg-shared-n2dl4  allocation: device=gpu-0
06:42:54.218  PreFilter.DynamicResources pod=p2 claim=repro-pg-shared-n2dl4  "reusing pending allocation" allocation: device=gpu-0
06:42:54.221  Reserve.DynamicResources   pod=p2 claim=repro-pg-shared-n2dl4  allocation: device=gpu-1   # <-- c-own's fresh result
06:42:54.222  Reserve.DynamicResources   pod=p2 claim=c-own                   allocation: device=gpu-0   # <-- shared's pending result
06:42:54.245  PreBind.DynamicResources   pod=p1 claim=repro-pg-shared-n2dl4  "preparing claim status update" (gpu-0 published)
06:47:17.296  PreBind.DynamicResources   pod=p2 ERROR "claim dra-crosswire-mokka/repro-pg-shared-n2dl4 got allocated elsewhere in the meantime"
```

```
Warning  FailedScheduling  pod/p2  running PreBind plugin "DynamicResources":
claim dra-crosswire-mokka/repro-pg-shared-n2dl4 got allocated elsewhere in the meantime
```

Run where `p2`'s PreBind won — the swapped results get persisted, p1 is the one that fails, then silently reuses the wrong device:

```
06:47:17.390  Reserve.DynamicResources   pod=p1 claim=repro-pg-shared-bgldq  allocation: device=gpu-0
06:47:17.390  PreFilter.DynamicResources pod=p2 claim=repro-pg-shared-bgldq  "reusing pending allocation" allocation: device=gpu-0
06:47:17.390  Reserve.DynamicResources   pod=p2 claim=repro-pg-shared-bgldq  allocation: device=gpu-1   # cross-wired
06:47:17.390  Reserve.DynamicResources   pod=p2 claim=c-own                   allocation: device=gpu-0   # cross-wired
06:47:17.414  PreBind.DynamicResources   pod=p2 claim=repro-pg-shared-bgldq  "preparing claim status update" (gpu-1 written first)
06:47:17.456  PreBind.DynamicResources   pod=p2 "Claim stored in assume cache" resourceVersion=1170468
06:47:17.478  PreBind.DynamicResources   pod=p1 ERROR "claim dra-crosswire-mokka/repro-pg-shared-bgldq got allocated elsewhere in the meantime"
              (p1 retries, reuses the already-allocated gpu-1 without selector validation, binds successfully)
```

**Anything else we need to know:**

Root cause as I read it, on current master (69a8e1ff315), `pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/dynamicresources/dynamicresources.go`:

Filter puts fresh allocation results first and pending (reused) results last:

```go
// line 1096
allocations = append(allocationResult, pendingResult...)
// allocations contains allocationResult followed by pendingResult.
// The first len(claimsToAllocate) elements match claimsToAllocate.
```

Reserve then consumes that slice **positionally**, zipped against the pod's claim list:

```go
// lines 1526-1531
allocIndex := 0
for index, claim := range state.claims.toAllocate() {
    allocation := &allocations.allocationResults[allocIndex]
    state.informationsForClaim[index].allocation = allocation
    ...
    allocIndex++
```

For `p2` the claim order is `[shared (pending), c-own (fresh)]` but the slice is `[fresh(gpu-1), pending(gpu-0)]`, so shared gets c-own's result and vice versa. Notably Filter also fills a UID-keyed `allocationsMap` right below line 1096, which *is* correct — Reserve just doesn't use it for this. PreBind then writes `state.informationsForClaim[index].allocation` into the claim status (bindClaim, line 1785); the guard at lines 1887-1889 (`claim.Status.Allocation != nil` → "allocated elsewhere") only helps when the correct pod wrote first, it cannot detect the wrong pod winning the race.

So the minimal fix is presumably to build `allocations` in the pod's claim order (or have Reserve consume `allocationsMap` by claim UID instead of by index).

Two things I want to flag so they don't muddy the water:

- The `allocated elsewhere in the meantime` event *by itself* is the documented, by-design retry for shared claims (the comment around line 1478 says exactly this: "If it fails at that time, some other pod was faster and we have to try again"). The bug is not the event — it is that Reserve hands each pod a mismatched expectation in the first place, which is what makes the event fire with both pods doing exactly what they were told, and what allows the wrong device to be persisted when the race goes the other way.
- Unrelated to this bug: on this alpha kubelet, pods using workload-level claims stay in ContainerCreating with `FailedPrepareDynamicResources … ResourceClaim was not created for Pod (Pod is not owner)`. That is an alpha-feature wart of `DRAWorkloadResourceClaims`, not related to the scheduler issue above.

**Environment information:**

- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.36.5+rke2r1 (client & server)
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: single VMware virtual machine
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Ubuntu 26.04 LTS
- Kernel (e.g: `uname -a`): Linux 7.0.0-42-generic x86_64
- Install tools: rke2, with the feature-gate / runtime-config patch shown above
- Network plugin and version: n/a
- Others: GPUs simulated with nvml-mock (mokka) 0.6.0, `gpu.count=2`; NVIDIA GPU DRA driver helm chart 0.5.1; scheduler logs captured at `-v=5`, no code patches anywhere

title: [Failing test] Pod InPlace Resize Memory-Backed Volume e2e tests fail on gci-gce-nftables and ppc64le: tmpfs remount drops noswap
body:
### Which jobs are failing?

- ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-nftables (COS 125, kernel 6.12.55)
- ci-kubernetes-e2e-ppc64le-default (CentOS Stream 10, kernel 6.12.0-277.el10)
- ci-kubernetes-ppc64le-e2e-alpha-enabled-default

### Which tests are failing?

All six `[sig-node] Pod InPlace Resize Memory-Backed Volume [FeatureGate:InPlacePodVerticalScalingMemoryBackedVolumes] memory-backed emptyDir volume resize ...` tests, on every run:

- uncapped volume resize when container memory limit changes
- volume resize (upsize then downsize)
- volume resize + container resize (upsize then downsize)
- volume resize add sizeLimit then remove (nil)
- volume resize add sizeLimit then remove (zero value)
- volume resize sizeLimit exceeding pod memory limit is capped to pod limit

### Since when has it been failing?

2026-11-06. gci-gce-nftables was green at v1.38.0-beta.0.52 ([2118744390380818432](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-nftables/2118744390380818432)) and red at v1.38.0-beta.0.96 ([2118834987984752640](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-nftables/2118834987984752640)). #141807 (feature to Beta, enabled by default) merged inside that window, so the tests started to run in jobs without alpha gates. The alpha-enabled ppc64le job was already failing them.

### Testgrid link

- https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-network-gce#periodic-network-nftables,%20google-gce
- https://testgrid.k8s.io/ibm-ppc64le-e2e#ci-kubernetes-e2e-ppc64le-default
- https://testgrid.k8s.io/ibm-ppc64le-e2e#ci-kubernetes-ppc64le-e2e-alpha-enabled-default

Triage clusters: [610e226ffa7732a8e1d4](https://storage.googleapis.com/k8s-triage/index.html#610e226ffa7732a8e1d4), [9ce935dae5434d87d10e](https://storage.googleapis.com/k8s-triage/index.html#9ce935dae5434d87d10e)

### Reason for failure (if possible)

The resize never completes. Pod status carries:

```
failed to resize volume mem-vol: mount failed: exit status 32
Mounting arguments:  -t tmpfs -o remount,size=262144000 tmpfs /var/lib/kubelet/pods/.../volumes/kubernetes.io~empty-dir/mem-vol
Output: mount: ...: mount point not mounted or bad option.
```

The node kernel log gives the real reason at every attempt ([kern.log](https://gcsweb.k8s.io/gcs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-nftables/2120647950815203328/artifacts/bootstrap-e2e-minion-group-t1pf/kern.log), and the ppc64le build log prints it directly through util-linux 2.40):

```
tmpfs: Cannot enable swap on remount if it was disabled on first mount
```

The kubelet mounts tmpfs volumes with `noswap` on kernels 6.4 and newer. `ResizeEphemeralVolume` ([empty_dir_linux.go#L138](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ba112edc01b2f68abb80669457f1fa32a5e852a1/pkg/volume/emptydir/empty_dir_linux.go#L138)) remounts with `remount,size=N` only. Kernels before 6.12.60 and 6.6.118 reject that with EINVAL. Linux commit [3cd1548a278c](https://git.kernel.org/linus/3cd1548a278c7d6a9bdef1f1866e7cf66bfd3518) (v6.18-rc7) removed the check. The kind jobs and the GCE presubmit pass because their kernels (GKE 6.12.105, Ubuntu 24.04 6.8) carry the fix.

### Anything else we need to know?

Every memory-backed emptyDir resize fails on affected kernels, not only in CI. Adding `noswap` to a remount of a mount that lacks it is rejected by every kernel (`Cannot disable swap on remount`), so the fix has to repeat `noswap` only when the live mount has it. Fix ready in dims/kubernetes branch [memvol-resize-noswap](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/compare/master...dims:kubernetes:memvol-resize-noswap).

### Relevant SIG(s)

/sig node
/kind failing-test
/area kubelet
